signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：glob是AI进行文件发现和批量操作的核心工具，在WSL2环境下彻底不可用，严重影响Windows+WSL2用户的工作流。wasm-simd不支持导致底层WebAssembly解析失败。

source_issues.title: Glob tool fails with WebAssembly parsing error in WSL2
source_issues.evidence: WebAssembly.Module parsing error at byte 175: wasm-simd is not enabled. Glob tool completely broken for ANY pattern in WSL2 (Ubuntu/Linux kernel 6.6.87.2 on WSL2). Other tools (read, edit, bash) unaffected. Blocks AI's file discovery capability.

signals.topic: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field, causing 400 API errors in agentic multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: When the API returns a tool search error, ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() re-serializes it but the omitzero tag on ErrorCode causes the field to be dropped if its value is the empty string. The resulting malformed payload triggers a 400 from the API on the next agentic-loop turn, breaking multi-turn conversations that use tool search.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug: multi-turn agentic conversations that use tool search will crash with a 400 error on the turn following a tool search error. The root cause is a precise type-system issue (omitzero tag + zero-value enum) that causes a required field to silently disappear. The user must write a raw JSON passthrough workaround, which is a significant degradation for a core SDK use case (agentic loops). Count=1 in this file, so P1 rather than P0.

source_issues.title: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field via omitzero
source_issues.evidence: API returns error_code in tool_search_tool_result; ToParam() re-serializes with omitzero tag which drops the field when value is empty string; subsequent API call receives 400 because error_code is required; workaround requires raw JSON passthrough; also confirmed in v1.34.0 and v1.35.0; related to same class of bug in #242 (WebSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam())

signals.topic: Official documentation examples use SDK types that do not exist, blocking users from trying Managed Agents feature
signals.summary: The official documentation at platform.claude.com includes Go code examples for creating sessions and sending events with Managed Agents that reference types which are absent from the installed SDK (v1.35.1), including SendEventsParamsUnion, BetaManagedAgentsUserDefineOutcomeEventParams, and related union types.
aliases: SDK types missing from Go examples
signals.review_reason: A user following the official documentation cannot compile or run the provided Go example because referenced types are missing from the SDK. This directly blocks usage of the Managed Agents feature, a key product capability. While count=1 (single report), the nature of the issue — uncompilable official examples for a major new feature — makes it a clear user pain point warranting P1. Not P2 because it is a documentation correctness failure that affects every user who tries this feature.

source_issues.title: Examples in documentation use types that don't exist.
source_issues.evidence: User installed v1.35.1 and copied Go example from official docs (platform.claude.com); compilation fails because BetaSessionNewParamsAgentUnion.OfString, SendEventsParamsUnion, BetaManagedAgentsUserDefineOutcomeEventParams, and BetaManagedAgentsUserDefineOutcomeEventParamsRubricUnion do not exist in the SDK; user is blocked from using the Managed Agents feature entirely

signals.topic: Structured Output schema generator ignores Java nullability annotations, treating all fields as required
signals.summary: When using outputConfig with Java classes, the schema generator ignores @Nullable and Optional types, placing all fields in the required array. This causes LLMs to hallucinate placeholder values (e.g. "null" strings, empty strings, dashes) for genuinely optional fields, degrading structured output quality.
aliases: Java nullability annotations ignored in schema generation
structured output schema treats all Java fields as required
signals.review_reason: Confirmed functional failure of structured output feature. The schema generator incorrectly marks all Java class fields as required regardless of nullability annotations, directly causing LLM hallucination of placeholder values (null strings, empty strings, dashes). This is not a theoretical concern — the user's structured output data is corrupted by the SDK's incorrect schema generation, making the feature unreliable for production use.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional are all ignored by the schema generator. The generated JSON Schema marks all fields as required, causing the LLM to hallucinate values to satisfy schema constraints. Clear functional degradation of structured output feature.

signals.topic: MCP Streamable HTTP transport incompatibility — tool call results silently lost or blocked
signals.summary: CMA's MCP client falls back to Streamable HTTP after SSE probe fails, but silently drops tool call results in relay (#1405), and is entirely incompatible with SSE-dropped servers (#1383). Both leave agents reporting false tool failures or never using the MCP server at all.
signals.review_reason: Three issues across MCP transport layers all block the same user workflow: calling tools via MCP in Managed Agents. #1405 produces false failure reports to users (#1405). #1383 makes entire MCP servers unusable (#1383). #1357 breaks the streaming interface entirely for all managed agents consumers. All three are reproducible with clear steps and produce complete functional blockages — no partial workaround exists at the user level for #1405 and #1383.

source_issues.title: CMA: Tool call results silently lost when server returns 406 on GET /mcp SSE probe
source_issues.evidence: Server-side tool execution succeeds (POST /mcp 200) but agent reports 'error communicating with Snowflake' — results are silently dropped during Streamable HTTP fallback. FastMCP 2.14.2/3.2.4 servers are spec-compliant (Streamable HTTP only).

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint 2026-04-01; CMA MCP client only supports SSE, causing complete initialization failure for all Apify users. 'SSE data line is not valid JSON' error. No client-side workaround.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Managed Agents: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() silently drops all events
source_issues.evidence: Stream.__stream__() hardcoded to Messages API event names; all managed agents events (session.status_*, agent.message, agent.tool_use, agent.tool_result, etc.) are silently dropped. Zero events yielded from a 3-event stream. Workaround: polling via events.list(). Closed 2026-04-14.

signals.topic: beta.skills.list hard-capped at 100 items — prevents full enumeration and causes silent data loss / false 400 errors
signals.summary: client.beta.skills.list() returns at most 100 skills regardless of limit, has_more always false, no cursor. Accounts with >100 skills cannot enumerate their inventory, causing workflows that reconcile skills state to silently miss items and produce false 'duplicate display_title' 400 errors at create time.
signals.review_reason: count=2 with clear user impact: >100 skills cannot be enumerated (silent data loss), provisioning workflows fail with false 400 errors, and file garbage collection is impossible. Both issues are reproducible with provided test scripts. The two issues share a root cause (Skills API pagination missing) and compound each other.

source_issues.title: beta.skills.list hard-capped at 100 items with broken pagination (has_more always false, no cursor)
source_issues.evidence: Tested with limit=10/50/100/500/1000 — all return exactly 100 items. has_more=false with no next_page/after_id. The SDK auto-paginator terminates after first page. User's provisioning script misses ~20 skills (120 exist) causing false 400 duplicate errors and inability to look up skill_ids for deletion.

source_issues.title: Cannot GC orphan Files API files — skill→file linkage not exposed on skills.versions.retrieve
source_issues.evidence: ~1100 orphan files accumulating on account. skills.versions.retrieve returns no 'files' field, files.list returns no skill_id back-reference. Cannot safely delete orphans without breaking live skills. Compounded by #1391: even if file linkage is exposed, full skill enumeration is blocked by 100-item cap.

signals.topic: web_search_20250209 dynamic filtering causes excessive pause_turn at ~110 content blocks — blocks 50-60% of batch requests
signals.summary: When web_search_20250209 tool performs dynamic filtering internally, the server-side sampling loop hits its 10-iteration limit and returns pause_turn with ~110 content blocks and no usable output. Affects 50-60% of production batch runs, wasting full token costs with no output. Workaround exists (allowed_callers:[direct]) but is undocumented and users don't know if it's stable.
signals.review_reason: count=1 but high real-world production impact: 50-60% of batch requests fail with no output while incurring full token costs. Batch of 35 requests takes 9+ hours instead of 38 min. Regression over time. Workaround (allowed_callers:[direct]) exists but is undocumented and stability unknown — users are dependent on an undocumented parameter for production batch processing.

source_issues.title: `web_search_20250209` dynamic filtering causes excessive `pause_turn` at ~110 content blocks — batch processing impractical
source_issues.evidence: Production batch runs (50+ requests): 55-60% hit pause_turn on first attempt with no usable output. Average time per request: 32 min (incl. retries) vs 46 seconds with workaround. Cost per failed attempt: $0.15-0.25 wasted. Only workaround is undocumented allowed_callers parameter. Regression: pause_turn rate increased from ~33% (early March) to ~60% (March 10).

signals.topic: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc compiled module missing
signals.summary: pdfplumber is documented as pre-installed in the code_execution_20250825 sandbox but fails immediately on import due to a missing mypyc-compiled charset_normalizer C extension (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '81d243bd2c585b0f4821__mypyc'). Users attempting PDF processing hit this error, forcing workarounds with pypdf.
signals.review_reason: Key functionality (PDF processing in code execution sandbox) is advertised as available but completely broken on import. Users following documented capabilities hit an immediate error with no ability to process PDFs. This is a mismatch between documented sandbox environment and actual runtime — a clear user-facing pain point.

source_issues.title: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing
source_issues.evidence: import pdfplumber immediately raises ModuleNotFoundError for mypyc-compiled extension. Dependency chain: pdfplumber -> pdfminer -> charset_normalizer. The hash-prefixed .so binary is missing from the sandbox image. pdfplumber is documented as pre-installed but completely unusable. Workaround: use pypdf instead.

signals.topic: pause_turn with web_search: documentation says re-submit response as-is, but API returns 400 — workflow broken
signals.summary: The server tools documentation instructs users to re-submit a paused response as-is to resume a turn after pause_turn with web_search. However, the API rejects this with a 400 error stating the web_search tool_use block was not paired with a result. The API's own validator rejects the block that the API itself produced and told users to send back.
signals.review_reason: count=1, single-repository, but represents a fundamental documentation vs. API contract mismatch that breaks a documented user workflow. Users following official docs hit a 400 from the API's own validator. This is a clear UX failure: the system tells users what to do and then rejects the correct response. Non-blocking but persistent.

source_issues.title: pause_turn with web_search: docs say re-submit response as-is, but API returns 400 — are we missing something?
source_issues.evidence: API returns pause_turn with unpaired server_tool_use (no web_search_tool_result). Re-submitting that content as instructed by docs produces: 'web_search tool use was found without a corresponding web_search_tool_result block' — 400 error. API validator contradicts its own documentation. Workaround: strip server_tool_use blocks, abandoning in-flight search state.

signals.topic: SSE ping events silently dropped by SDK, causing streaming reliability failures and false-positive watchdog aborts
signals.summary: The TypeScript SDK silently discards SSE ping events from the server stream (if (event === 'ping') continue). This prevents downstream clients—including Claude Code CLI—from distinguishing 'server actively thinking' from 'stream silently stalled'. The result is that streaming watchdogs built on top of the SDK fire false-positive aborts during normal extended-thinking operations (Opus with high effort can go silent for 60–120s between text deltas), and genuine hangs remain indistinguishable from normal operation. Claude Code users on Opus + extended thinking are hitting 'Stream idle timeout - partial response received' errors repeatedly (40+ reports in 24h on claude-code#46987), forcing process restarts to recover.
signals.review_reason: Main流程阻断: stream无限等待导致进程hang，用户工作丢失，已有40+用户在Claude Code上复现。根因明确(SDK丢弃ping事件)，有真实生产事故证据(#867 session f35c7c15)，跨仓库影响(claude-code)。3个issue全部指向同一根因，置信度极高。P0符合高频(count=3,跨仓)+主流程阻断+强证据。

source_issues.title: include ping and error in RawMessageStreamEvent
source_issues.evidence: SDK drops ping events with 'continue', preventing consumers from tracking server liveness. Open 11 months with collaborator acknowledgment (RobertCraigie: 'still valuable to receive ping events').

source_issues.title: bug/proposal: infinitely hanging clients breaking bigger/complex sessions. Proposal: add Streaming Idle Timeout
source_issues.evidence: Real production incident (session f35c7c15-802e-462b-b468-b000a96e40bb): stream stalled mid-response, process hung at 0% CPU indefinitely, 15+ minutes of lost productivity. Root cause: no ping events, no idle timeout. Existing timeouts (overall timeout, AbortController) both failed to detect the stall.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Ping-aware streaming watchdog (fixes #749, #867, and downstream Claude Code hangs)
source_issues.evidence: Cross-references Claude Code#46987 (40+ reports in 24h), #33949 (32 comments, SSE hangs indefinitely + ESC cannot cancel), #39755. Documents real logs showing 3 consecutive retries, all aborting at exactly 90s while server was sending pings the entire time.

signals.topic: JSON.parse unhandled crash when model outputs regex-like escape sequences in structured output
signals.summary: When Claude is asked to produce JSON containing regex-like patterns, Windows paths, or LaTeX (all containing escape sequences valid in their own context but not strict JSON), the streaming parser's JSON.parse call throws an unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the entire Node.js process. No recovery path exists for the application.
aliases: SyntaxError crash on regex in JSON
JSON parsing fails on model output
streaming parser crash invalid escape sequences
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断(崩溃): Node.js进程crash导致应用完全中断，热门场景(生成含regex/路径/LaTeX的JSON)完全不可用。unhandled rejection无任何恢复路径。虽有单仓单条issue，但根因明确(严格JSON.parse无容错)，review_reason给出强用户影响证据链(完整crash stack, 可复现场景)。

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with claude-sonnet-4-6 requesting JSON with regex \\d+\\.\\d+. Stack trace shows unhandled SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token at JSON.parse in MessageStream. Error propagates as unhandled rejection, crashing the Node.js process entirely. No recovery path.

signals.topic: toolRunner fails to propagate container.id across iterations, forcing broken workarounds that cause infinite loops
signals.summary: When using client-side betaTools alongside code_execution_20260120 in a streaming toolRunner loop, the container.id returned by the server is not forwarded into the next iteration's request, causing a hard 'container_id is required' API error. The available workaround—using setMessagesParams—either fails immediately (type mismatch) or corrupts accumulated message history, causing the model to enter an infinite duplicate tool-call loop. There is no working path to use client-side tools with code execution in a streaming toolRunner loop.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用: betaTools + code_execution组合的核心使用路径完全不可用，两个workaround均broken(直接报错或无限循环)。有官方'bug'标签。虽有单仓单条issue，但review_reason明确: 核心beta功能路径阻断，无任何workaround，属于SDK层面的明确bug而非feature request。

source_issues.title: Bug: toolRunner does not propagate container.id across iterations, and setMessagesParams causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: Two compounding bugs: (1) container.id not forwarded causes hard API error 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution'. (2) setMessagesParams workaround causes infinite tool-calling loop—the model repeatedly calls code_execution with identical inputs. No working path exists. Labeled 'bug' by reporter.

signals.topic: O(N²) string concatenation in MessageStream causes severe performance degradation on long responses
signals.summary: MessageStream accumulates streamed text using += string concatenation in a loop, which is O(N²) in JavaScript due to string immutability. For long responses (code generation, structured JSON output), performance degrades severely: 4K tokens takes ~16x longer than optimal, 10K tokens ~100x slower. This is a regression that makes long structured-output generation impractical.
signals.review_reason: 性能显著下降: 10K token响应慢100倍，热门场景(code generation, structured JSON output)严重受损。根因清晰(string +=)，有benchmark数据支撑。虽count=1且单仓，但P2已是最低优先级，符合'regression且有明确性能数据'的保留标准。

source_issues.title: perf(MessageStream): O(N²) complexity in text accumulation during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: Benchmark shows 1K vs 4K tokens should be 4x but is ~16x. At 10K tokens, ~100x slower than optimal. Root cause in MessageStream.ts: 'snapshot.content[i].text = (snapshot.content[i].text ?? '') + delta.text' creates new string on each iteration. Author offered PR with benchmarks.

signals.topic: docx and pptx Agent Skills fail silently during streaming with no error surfaced
signals.summary: When using Agent Skills with the container.skills parameter, the docx and pptx skills cause the stream to end without producing a Message, while pdf and xlsx work correctly. The failure surfaces as 'stream ended without producing a Message with role=assistant' but provides no actionable error. Users cannot use docx or pptx skills in streaming mode.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用: docx和pptx skill在streaming模式下完全不可用，而pdf/xlsx正常。6 comments表明用户持续受影响。虽有单仓单条issue，但skill功能是Managed Agents核心卖点之一，特定skill不可用属于关键功能缺失，review_reason给出可验证的对比测试数据。

source_issues.title: Agent Skills: docx and pptx skills fail silently with streaming
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows pdf and xlsx work, docx and pptx fail. Stream ends with 'stream ended without producing a Message with role=assistant'. 6 comments indicating ongoing investigation. Key functionality (docx/pptx skill support) not working in streaming mode.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport async task management broken: 100% CPU leak on query() exit, background task notification cross-turn leak, multi-context async blocked
signals.summary: The SubprocessCLITransport in subprocess_cli.py has a recurring async task management anti-pattern: (1) anyio task group not properly exited on query() completion causes 100% CPU spin via _deliver_cancellation, (2) TaskNotificationMessage from completed background tasks bleeds into the next receive_response() call, poisoning the next turn with a stale model response, (3) ClaudeSDKClient cannot be used across different async contexts (trio nurseries, asyncio task groups).
aliases: anyio task group cancel scope leak
signals.review_reason: Three issues, all confirmed, all caused by async task management problems in SubprocessCLITransport. #810 causes 100% CPU spin that hangs the process — a main-flow denial of service. #788 corrupts conversation state across turns, causing the model to respond to wrong inputs. #815 restricts fundamental SDK usage patterns. All three are repeated, well-documented failures with clear root cause in the same transport layer.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: SubprocessCLITransport has the same anyio.create_task_group() + manual __aenter__/__aexit__ anti-pattern that was fixed in query.py. Normal query() completion triggers cross-task cancel scope exit, cancelling the caller's task and pinning _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop.

source_issues.title: Background task notification leaks into next turn after receive_response()
source_issues.evidence: When a background task completes between turns, its TaskNotificationMessage leaks into the next receive_response() call. The model responds to the stale task notification instead of the new user prompt, corrupting the conversation.

source_issues.title: Ability to Use ClaudeSDK Client from multiple async contexts
source_issues.evidence: ClaudeSDKClient cannot be used across different async runtime contexts (different trio nurseries or asyncio task groups). Internal anyio task group for reading messages remains active from connect() until disconnect(), restricting usage to a single async context.

signals.topic: Opus 4.7 thinking visibility regression: SDK silently drops thinking.display config, causing empty thinking blocks
signals.summary: On Opus 4.7+ the API defaults thinking.display to 'omitted'. The SDK's SubprocessCLITransport only forwards thinking.type, silently dropping the display field, so CLI --thinking-display is never set. Users get empty ThinkingBlock.thinking and no thinking_delta events with no error signal. Additionally, SDK users who explicitly set thinking.type=enabled get a fatal API 400 error on Opus 4.7.
signals.review_reason: Two issues confirm a regression on Opus 4.7 where thinking content is invisible to SDK users. #831 is a silent data-loss bug: thinking blocks are always empty with no error, making extended thinking useless. #829 is a fatal API error for users who set thinking.type=enabled. Both are clear main-flow regressions that break a shipped feature.

source_issues.title: Opus 4.7 returns empty thinking text: ThinkingConfig.display not forwarded to CLI
source_issues.evidence: ThinkingBlock.thinking is always '' and no thinking_delta events arrive on Opus 4.7+ even with thinking={'type':'adaptive'}. _build_command silently drops the display key. Workaround requires a hidden CLI flag.

source_issues.title: Opus 4.7 + 0.1.58 = thinking.type.enabled errors?
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 error 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported for this model. Use thinking.type.adaptive' on Opus 4.7. SDK users who try to enable thinking get fatal API errors.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration broken: stdin closed before MCP handshake with string prompts; search_result content blocks silently dropped
signals.summary: When query() is called with a string prompt and mcp_servers, the transport closes stdin immediately after writing the message, before the CLI's MCP handshake. This causes a CLIConnectionError and prevents any MCP tool usage. Separately, MCP tool handlers returning search_result content blocks silently discard them, breaking RAG citations.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but related MCP integration failures. #817 is a hard block: any use of MCP servers with string prompts crashes immediately with a connection error. #574 silently destroys data: search_result blocks are dropped with no error, breaking a documented API feature (native citations). Both are regressions in core SDK functionality.

source_issues.title: query() + mcp_servers: string-prompt branch closes stdin before MCP handshake, not fixed by #731
source_issues.evidence: Calling query() with string prompt and mcp_servers raises CLIConnectionError: ProcessTransport is not ready for writing during MCP server handshake. transport.end_input() is called unconditionally after string-mode user message, before CLI can register the MCP server.

source_issues.title: search_result content blocks silently dropped by MCP tool result handler
source_issues.evidence: Custom @tool handlers returning search_result content blocks have those blocks silently discarded. message_parser.py only handles text/thinking/tool_use/tool_result blocks. Claude receives empty tool result and cannot produce citations for RAG workflows.

signals.topic: API-key users silently overcharged: bundled CLI predates 1h cache TTL opt-in, costing real money in production
signals.summary: SDK v0.1.59 ships CLI 2.1.105, but the ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var that enables 1-hour token cache TTL was only added in CLI 2.1.108. API-key users cannot opt into the 1h tier. Production sessions of 16–60 minutes accumulate massive unnecessary cost by being billed at 5-minute TTL rates.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial harm: users were billed at a higher cache tier than they should have been for 8 months in production. This is not a crash but a silent cost leak that compounds on exactly the SDK's primary workload (long-running agent sessions). Priority P0 is justified by the documented monetary impact across hundreds of thousands of agent turns.

source_issues.title: API-key users silently stuck on 5m cache TTL: bundled CLI in v0.1.59 predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H opt-in
source_issues.evidence: Users report 8 months of production use with cache writes billed at 5-minute tier instead of 1-hour tier. Long agent sessions (16–60 min) compound this cost. Developer relations claimed prompt caching savings were automatic for SDK customers, but this is false for API-key users.

signals.topic: StructuredOutput tool non-deterministically wraps output in 'output' field, causing schema validation failures
signals.summary: The StructuredOutput tool intermittently wraps the response in an extra {'output': {...}} wrapper, causing schema validation to fail. This is non-deterministic — identical prompts can produce either format. When validation fails, the model receives conflicting error messages and degrades its output (e.g., 47 items reduced to 1).
signals.review_reason: A single issue but with 10+ comments confirming broad user impact. The non-determinism means production agents using StructuredOutput cannot be trusted to produce reliable results. When the wrapper appears, the model itself degrades output quality in response to the confusing error. This is a production reliability issue that makes structured outputs unreliable.

source_issues.title: [BUG] StructuredOutput tool wraps data in 'output' field causing schema validation to fail
source_issues.evidence: Intermittent output wrapping produces validation error 'root: must NOT have additional properties'. 10+ comments with users experiencing the issue. Model responds to validation errors by reducing output from 47 items to 1 item. Non-deterministic: same prompt succeeds or fails randomly.

signals.topic: SDK closes stdin stream after first result, causing MCP tools and hook callbacks to fail with 'Stream closed' error
signals.summary: When using async-iterable prompts with bidirectional controls (hooks/SDK MCP/canUseTool/elicitation), the SDK's streamInput() calls transport.endInput() after the first result, closing stdin. Subsequent Monitor task-notification continuations then fail with 'Stream closed' for all MCP tools and PostToolUse/hook callbacks.
aliases: Stream closed cascade after first result
stdin EOF causes MCP tool failures after Monitor task-notification
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime bug: async-iterable prompt users with MCP tools or hooks encounter cascading 'Stream closed' failures on queued task-notification continuations. The failure is reproducible, blocks MCP tool usage, and is explicitly demonstrated with a minimal fake-process repro plus real session timestamps. Count=1 because this specific stdin-closure cascade scenario appears in one issue.

source_issues.title: SDK closes stdin after first result while CLI can continue from Monitor task-notification, causing Stream closed cascade
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with minimal fake-process repro showing stdin ends after first result. Real session log: MCP tool call at 04:52:17.796Z returns 'Error: Stream closed'; all subsequent MCP tools and hook-backed built-ins fail identically. Process/session stays alive but control channel is broken.

signals.topic: PostToolUse callback hooks silently discard return value; updatedMCPToolOutput not persisted to transcript
signals.summary: When all PostToolUse hooks are JavaScript callbacks (no shell/agent/function hooks mixed in), the SDK takes a 'callback-only fast path' that calls the hook but discards its return value entirely. The updatedMCPToolOutput from the hook response is never yielded, so the live API call does not see the replacement and the session transcript JSONL retains the original tool response.
aliases: PostToolUse callback return value silently dropped
MCP tool output override not propagated via callback-only fast path
hookSpecificOutput.updatedMCPToolOutput discarded in callback fast path
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed SDK bug where PostToolUse callback hooks fail silently to update MCP tool output. Users who rely on callback-only hook registration get zero feedback that their output modifications are discarded — the transcript silently retains original values. The root cause is explicitly traced in source code (Xh function, two distinct code paths). Requires non-trivial workaround (external TOON encoding). Count=1.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse callback hooks: return value (updatedMCPToolOutput) silently discarded, never persisted to transcript
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in SDK source: in Xh function, callback-only fast path calls hook but discards return value and returns without yielding. The feature works only when at least one non-callback hook is present (full FoY processing path). Workaround required TOON-encoding external MCP tool results at transcript persist time.

signals.topic: Manual session interruption (interrupt()) is flaky and unreliable in production
signals.summary: The interrupt() method on the SDK instance intermittently fails to pause active sessions. In affected sessions, interrupt() is called multiple times over several minutes without reaching the expected completion path (no 'interrupt() completed' log). Sessions appear not to pause reliably, leaving users unable to control long-running operations.
aliases: interrupt() call fails intermittently without error
signals.review_reason: Intermittent session interruption failure is a real user pain point: users cannot reliably abort long-running SDK sessions. Logs show multiple interrupt() calls spanning 4+ minutes without completion, while successful cases complete in milliseconds. The intermittent nature (most sessions stop successfully) makes this especially insidious. Count=1.

source_issues.title: manual user pause is flaky
source_issues.evidence: Real production logs provided: failed case shows interrupt() called at 09:15:28 repeatedly for 4+ minutes with no 'interrupt() completed' log. Successful case shows interrupt() completed within milliseconds. Most sessions stop successfully, but intermittent failures leave users unable to abort runaway sessions.

signals.topic: Programmatic options.env is ignored when ~/.claude/settings.json contains an env field
signals.summary: Environment variables passed via options.env do not override values in ~/.claude/settings.json, contradicting documented behavior. The SDK uses the settings.json value instead of the programmatically provided one, regardless of settingSources configuration.
aliases: options.env not overriding settings.json env values
API key from settings.json used instead of programmatically provided key
signals.review_reason: A configuration bug that actively breaks multi-tenant and development workflows: users cannot programmatically set API keys when settings.json is present, forcing them to modify their Claude Code CLI config to use the SDK. This is a clear experience degradation with a documented workaround that creates new problems. Count=1.

source_issues.title: Programmatic options.env does not override env values in ~/.claude/settings.json
source_issues.evidence: Step-by-step reproduction provided: setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via options.env vs settings.json. Workaround requires manually removing env field from settings.json, which disrupts the developer's interactive Claude Code setup. Affects multi-tenant apps, custom base URLs, and any developer using both CLI and SDK.

signals.topic: V2 Session API (unstable_v2_createSession) silently ignores permissionMode, cwd, settingSources, allowedTools options
signals.summary: The V2 Session API constructor hardcodes ProcessTransport options (permissionMode: 'default', empty allowedTools/settingSources/mcpServers) instead of forwarding from SDKSessionOptions. Critical server-side options are silently dropped, making V2 sessions unusable for headless deployments, CI pipelines, and Slack bots where permission bypass and workspace scoping are required.
aliases: V2 session silently ignores server-side required options
signals.review_reason: V2 session API is fundamentally broken for its primary use case: server-side deployments. permissionMode bypass, cwd, and allowedTools are silently ignored — the session spawns with defaults that make it useless for headless environments. This is a key functionality failure, not just a degraded experience. Count=1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] V2 Session API (unstable_v2_createSession) ignores permissionMode, cwd, settingSources, allowedTools options
source_issues.evidence: Source-level root cause identified: SessionImpl constructor in sdk.mjs hardcodes values instead of reading from options. ProcessTransport.initialize() already handles all these options correctly but never receives them. Related issues #154, #160, #171 all stem from the same pattern. Makes V2 sessions fundamentally unusable for server/headless deployments.

signals.topic: execution_file not written to disk when SDK throws an error (e.g., error_max_turns, API errors, unsupported model flags)
signals.summary: When the Claude SDK throws at any point — including error_max_turns, API 400 errors, or unsupported model flags — the execution_file output at $RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json is never created. Downstream steps that depend on structured execution data (cost, turn count, duration, tool error counts) receive no data. This is caused by the writeFile call being placed after the try/catch re-throw in run-claude-sdk.ts.
aliases: SDK error prevents execution file write
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine workflow-runtime data loss issue. When the SDK throws (error_max_turns, API errors, model flag incompatibility), the execution_file is never written, leaving downstream consumers with no structured diagnostic data. Two distinct issue reports confirm this. The root cause (writeFile after re-throw) is clearly identified in both.

source_issues.title: execution_file output not written when SDK throws on error_max_turns
source_issues.evidence: The file at $RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json is never created when SDK throws. Downstream steps extracting cost, turn count, duration, tool error counts get no data. The messages array IS populated up to the point of failure but is lost because writeFile is unreachable.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.7 not working with latest action v1.0.97
source_issues.evidence: SDK throws with API 400 invalid_request_error for claude-opus-4.7 due to unsupported thinking.type.enabled flag. The catch block re-throws before execution_file write, producing the same silent data loss as issue 1226.

signals.topic: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths (CLAUDE.md, etc.) are symlinks, introduced in v1.0.89
signals.summary: Since v1.0.89, the action crashes during the 'Restoring sensitive files from origin/master' step when any SENSITIVE_PATH is a symlink. cpSync with dereference:false tries to recreate the symlink rather than copy file contents, failing with ENOENT. The only workaround is pinning to v1.0.88.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed reports of the same crash with identical root cause (cpSync dereference:false on symlinks). Introduced in v1.0.89 and affects any repo using symlinks for CLAUDE.md or other sensitive files. Workaround requires pinning to v1.0.88, forcing users to stay on an older version. This is a common pattern in monorepos and documentation systems.

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks

signals.topic: Cursor Agent authentication does not persist in Goose2 after navigation
signals.summary: In Goose2 desktop app, signing in to Cursor Agent appears successful but authentication does not persist when navigating away and returning to the screen, requiring repeated login. The agent also inconsistently appears in the available agents list.
aliases: Goose2 agent auth session not persisted
Cursor Agent sign-in state lost on navigation
signals.review_reason: Clear functional regression in Goose2: agent authentication fails to persist across navigation, making the Cursor Agent feature unreliable. Users cannot use the agent feature without repeated sign-ins, which is a significant degradation of the multi-agent experience.

source_issues.title: agent auth does not persist for Cursor Agent in Goose2

aliases: gemini-acp provider not found in stable release
signals.review_reason: Docs/runtime mismatch causes setup failure for users following official documentation. Users attempting to use gemini-acp as documented immediately hit 'Unknown provider: gemini-acp' error. This is a primary workflow blocker for users trying to set up Gemini via ACP.

source_issues.title: v1.30.0 docs/runtime mismatch: docs advertise gemini-acp, but stable Goose reports "Unknown provider: gemini-acp"

Root cause: PR #8000 added gemini-acp, PR #8129 replaced it with gemini_oauth, but docs were not updated. User following official documentation gets immediate failure.

This is not a rare edge case; it affects every new install.

signals.summary: The Qwen3-coder-plus model regressed and now returns 400 invalid_parameter_error on every request in both VS Code and JetBrains/Rider IDEs.
signals.review_reason: A confirmed regression where a previously-working model is now completely unusable across multiple IDE platforms (VS Code and JetBrains). The user explicitly identifies this as a recent regression. count=2 confirms it is reproducible and not isolated to one environment.

source_issues.title: Recent Regression — 400 Bad Request with qwen3-coder-plus
source_issues.evidence: Model previously stable, now fails every request with 400 invalid_parameter_error in the VS Code extension. Error persists across restarts even for trivial prompts.

source_issues.title: Error when trying to query Qwen

signals.topic: Cline in PHPStorm: persistent 5-10 second stalling/freezing between agent commands
signals.summary: After a previous stalling fix, PHPStorm users still experience severe delays (5-10 seconds) between agent command outputs, making multi-step tasks extremely slow. VS Code is not affected.
signals.review_reason: Major UX degradation in the JetBrains platform: 5-10 second delays between command outputs make multi-step agentic tasks impractical. The issue is confirmed by GPU monitoring, affects multiple team members, and has been explicitly linked to a regression from a prior fix. Combined with the inability to cherry-pick files (#10275), it effectively disables Cline in PHPStorm.

source_issues.title: Still stalling/freezing in PHPstorm after fix for stalling due to text rendering
source_issues.evidence: 5-10 second delays between agent commands confirmed by watching GPU load on fast AI box outputting 100 tokens/sec. VS Code version runs 4-5x faster with sub-second delays. Multiple team members affected. Also causes Cline to halt mid-session when too many files loaded in context. Combined with #10275 (cannot cherry-pick files), Cline is completely broken in PHPStorm for this user.

signals.topic: Cline in PHPStorm: incorrect/unreadable colors with dark program theme + light editor theme
signals.summary: Color rendering in PHPStorm is inconsistent when using a dark program theme with a light editor theme, resulting in unreadable text in Cline UI.
signals.review_reason: UI rendering bug causes unreadable text in a specific but common theme combination (dark program theme + light editor). While not a crash, unreadable text in the primary interaction surface (chat/output) blocks effective use of the extension in affected theme setups.

source_issues.title: incorrect colors in CLine in PHPstorm when in dark mode with light editor theme
source_issues.evidence: With a dark grey program theme and light editor theme, CLine renders with mixed colors that don't match either theme, resulting in unreadable text. Other JetBrains plugins do not have this issue. Dark-on-dark themes work fine; the problem is specifically with mismatched theme combinations.

signals.topic: Cline in PHPStorm: Cannot add files or folders — 'no results found' always shown

This is not a minor UX issue — it blocks the entire core workflow of reading and modifying files. Confirmed across two PHPStorm versions.

source_issues.title: Cannot add files or folders in PHPstorm 2026.1
source_issues.evidence: Adding files or folders always returns 'no results found' message. This makes Cline completely unusable in PHPStorm since the agent cannot read project files. Reproduced on both PHPStorm 2026.1 and 2025.3.4. User states 'this makes Cline unusable to me.'

signals.topic: Continue UI fails to render correctly in code-server via Firefox browser
signals.summary: Continue's UI does not render properly when accessed through Firefox desktop connecting to code-server. This occurs across multiple Continue versions (1.2.21 through 1.3.37) and code-server v4, making Continue unusable in this specific browser/IDE combination.
signals.review_reason: Two separate reports confirm Continue is broken in Firefox + code-server configuration. Issue 12135 identifies the root cause (Firefox v149 security headers blocking CSS), issue 11932 shows broader rendering failure. This is a confirmed UX break for a non-trivial user segment running code-server with Firefox.

source_issues.title: code-server rendering in Firefox desktop
source_issues.evidence: Continue window does not render correctly in code-server via desktop Firefox. Tested across Continue v1.3.37 and v1.2.21 with code-server v4.112.0. User is blocked from using Continue in this configuration.

source_issues.title: CSS won't load on Firefox v149 in code-server
source_issues.evidence: Firefox v149's stricter security settings cause index.css to be blocked via Sec-Fetch-Mode: no-cors header, resulting in NS_ERROR_UNKNOWN_HOST. CSS fails to load, leaving Continue unstyled and likely non-functional in Firefox code-server. Affects code-server users on Linux/Fedora 43.

signals.topic: VS Code extension host terminates unexpectedly, crashing Continue
signals.summary: The Continue VS Code extension's host process terminates unexpectedly, causing the extension to crash and making the tool unusable mid-session. User reports on macOS with VS Code 1.113.0 and Continue 1.2.22 with no workaround available.
signals.review_reason: Extension host crash directly blocks the user's entire workflow in VS Code. While only 1 issue, the crash is described as the extension host terminating unexpectedly, which is a severe main-flow interruption with no documented workaround.

source_issues.title: Extension host terminated unexpectedly (continue.continue)
source_issues.evidence: Extension host terminated unexpectedly on macOS VS Code, Continue 1.2.22. No reproduction steps provided but clearly blocks the user's entire workflow.

signals.topic: Local autocomplete completely broken when using LM Studio models via VS Code on macOS

aliases: inline completion not working for local models
signals.review_reason: Local autocomplete is a core feature of Continue for local model users. Complete breakage means users cannot use the inline completion feature that is the primary value proposition for local/LM Studio setups. Only 1 issue but impact is severe — entire feature class is non-functional.

source_issues.title: Local Autocomplete Broken!
source_issues.evidence: User reports LM Studio shows logs for every code change but autocomplete never triggers. Affects local model users on macOS VS Code. LM Studio vA.5.0.0 with qwen3.5-35b-a3b model, Continue 1.2.22. The core autocomplete feature is completely non-functional.

signals.topic: Qwen 3.5 and Gemma 4 models cannot call tools, breaking agent functionality
signals.summary: Qwen 3.5 9B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B models via LM Studio produce malformed tool calls that Continue cannot parse. Tool calls appear in the model's thinking output rather than being registered, acting as message terminators and breaking all agent/tool-dependent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Tool calling is the core of Continue's agentic capabilities. When tools cannot be called, the agent becomes a stateless chat with no ability to read/write files or execute commands. The model families mentioned (Qwen 3.5, Gemma 4) are widely used local models. This is a clear main-flow functional break.

source_issues.title: Qwen 3.5 and Gemma 4 can't call tools
source_issues.evidence: User on macOS + VS Code + LM Studio reports that tool_call XML tags appear verbatim in model's thinking output instead of being registered as tool invocations. This means the agent cannot perform any tool-using action (file search, code edit, etc.), completely breaking the agent workflow for these two model families.

signals.topic: Add Model UI displays stale models from the previously selected provider after dynamic fetch resolves late
signals.summary: Switching providers in the Add Model UI before a dynamic model fetch completes causes the previously selected provider's models to appear under the newly selected provider. This can lead to users selecting or configuring the wrong model, resulting in failed requests or cost waste.
aliases: stale models in Add Model UI
wrong provider models shown after switch
signals.review_reason: Clear bug with identified root cause in async state handling. While it doesn't crash the extension, it leads to users configuring wrong models (wasted API calls, cost loss) and degraded trust in the Add Model UX. Precise reproduction steps and affected code location provided.

source_issues.title: Add Model UI can show stale models from a previously selected provider after dynamic fetch resolves late
source_issues.evidence: Race condition in AddModelForm.tsx: when user switches provider before a dynamic fetch resolves, the stale response overwrites the correct provider's model list. This leads to selecting/configuring the wrong model. Root cause is stale closure over selectedProvider. Has clear reproduction steps.

signals.topic: output_pydantic / response_model regression breaks tool calling on non-OpenAI LLMs (vLLM, LiteLLM)
signals.summary: Since v1.9.0, Task.output_pydantic is mapped to response_model and passed into the agent executor tool-calling loop on every iteration. For vLLM and LiteLLM-backed models, tools are completely skipped — the model returns structured JSON directly and _run() methods are never called. LiteLLM path additionally bypasses tools entirely via InternalInstructor. This is a confirmed regression from pre-v1.9.0 behavior.
aliases: response_model causes tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
output_pydantic regression blocks tool execution loop
JSON false positive parsing with output_pydantic
TypeError json.loads on PydanticModel with ConditionalTask + guardrail
signals.review_reason: Critical regression affecting all non-OpenAI LLM users (vLLM, LiteLLM, any OpenAI-compatible provider). Tools are silently skipped — the main agent workflow mechanism is broken. Three separate issues confirm the output_pydantic path is broken across different scenarios: tool calling loop regression (#5472), JSON false positives (#5460), and TypeError in ConditionalTask path (#5458). All three share the root cause of mishandled output_pydantic in the converter/executor path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] output_pydantic / response_model leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: Tools _run() methods are never called when output_pydantic is set. Verified with vLLM-served Qwen3.5-27B. LiteLLM path bypasses tools via InternalInstructor. Regression from v1.9.0. curl proof shows tools skipped with response_format present.

source_issues.title: [BUG] output_pydantic JSON substring identification has false positives with GraphQL and look-alike JSON
source_issues.evidence: Regex pattern in converter.py matches curly braces in GraphQL schemas as JSON, causing pydantic_core.ValidationError. Stack trace shows json.loads failed on GraphQL type syntax. Affects any output_pydantic task with structured text.

source_issues.title: [BUG] TypeError: JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not PydanticModel when combining ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context
source_issues.evidence: When ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrail references a context task with output_pydantic, CrewAI calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object instead of its serialized JSON string. TypeError crashes the crew. Full reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: MCP servers with >10 tools or recursive schemas cause recursion depth exceeded / schema corruption errors
signals.summary: Two issues confirm MCP schema handling is broken for realistic workloads. Issue #5474: MCP servers exposing >10 tools crash with RuntimeError: maximum recursion depth exceeded at tool_resolver.py#L447. Issue #5490: even after partial fix #5478, recursive $ref schemas still degrade to {} during sanitization and fail with JsonRefError later. Tree/graph-like MCP tool inputs (realistic pattern for enterprise servers) are unusable.
aliases: MCP server >10 tools recursion depth exceeded
signals.review_reason: MCP server integration is a key product feature. Realistic enterprise MCP servers (like ms-365-mcp-server, Atlassian MCP) expose >10 tools and tree/graph-like schemas. Two related issues confirm the problem is persistent across versions. Users must avoid realistic MCP servers or work around with alternate frameworks.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCP servers over 10 tools causes maximum recursion depth exceeded error
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: maximum recursion depth exceeded at tool_resolver.py#L447. ms-365-mcp-server exposes >10 tools. Reproduction with full code. CrewAI 1.14.1, Python 3.12. Pydantic AI handles the same server correctly. Blocking for enterprise MCP servers.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Incomplete follow-up fix for recursive MCP schemas after #5478
source_issues.evidence: Partial fix #5478 shipped in 1.14.2rc1 but recursive $ref schemas still fail. sanitize_tool_params_for_anthropic_strict degrades children.items to {}, and create_model_from_schema() fails with JsonRefError. Schema is silently corrupted rather than failing clearly.

signals.topic: Checkpoint TUI restore/fork path ignores Flow checkpoints and JSON listing misses branch subdirectories
signals.summary: Two checkpoint CLI/TUI issues. #5492: The TUI restore/fork dispatch path is hard-coded to Crew.from_checkpoint() / Crew.fork(), completely bypassing Flow.from_checkpoint() / Flow.fork() — Flow checkpoints selected in the TUI have no execution path. #5491: JSON checkpoint discovery uses flat glob patterns (location/*.json) that fail to find valid checkpoints stored under branch subdirectories (e.g., .checkpoints/fork/<branch>/). Both affect the recently added checkpoint forking and TUI feature.
aliases: Checkpoint TUI only works for Crew checkpoints not Flow
Checkpoint JSON discovery misses branch subdirectory layout
signals.review_reason: Checkpoint TUI is a core workflow feature for state recovery and branching. When Flow checkpoints cannot be restored from the TUI and valid JSON checkpoints are invisible, users lose the ability to resume from state — a primary use case of the checkpoint system. Affects the recently shipped checkpoint forking feature.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Checkpoint TUI restore/fork path is Crew-only for Flow checkpoints
source_issues.evidence: Local reproduction with stubbed TUI selection shows crew_fork:1, crew_resume:1, flow_fork:0, flow_resume:0. checkpoint_tui.py hard-codes Crew.from_checkpoint() / Crew.fork(). Flow checkpoints selected in TUI have no restore/fork path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] JSON checkpoint listing/info ignores branch subdirectories
source_issues.evidence: checkpoint_cli.py uses flat globs (location/*.json) for _list_json() and _info_json_latest(). Valid checkpoints under branch subdirectories (./checkpoints/fork/<branch>/) are invisible. Reproduction shows _list_json(root) returns [] for valid checkpoints.

signals.topic: Container startup crashes when LLM call fails during module import in ChatWithCrewFlow
signals.summary: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ triggers synchronous blocking LLM calls via crewai.cli.crew_chat module BEFORE uvicorn binds its HTTP port. Any LLM failure (500, rate-limit, network blip, invalid creds, timeout) causes the Python process to crash with exit code 1. In orchestrated environments (Railway, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, Fly.io), the platform marks the deploy failed and rolls back — service is completely unavailable.
aliases: LLM call at module import time crashes container
ChatWithCrewFlow init blocks on LLM causing container failure
signals.review_reason: Service becomes completely unavailable at container startup. Any transient LLM failure (500, rate-limit, timeout, network blip) causes hard crash before HTTP server listens. Verified with full stack trace on Railway deployment. Blocks all AG-UI / CopilotKit / FastAPI deployments using the recommended integration.

source_issues.title: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ makes blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers on any LLM hiccup
source_issues.evidence: Stack trace shows APIError from LLM crash during module import. Container exits with code 1, never binds port, orchestrator health check fails, deploy rolls back. Affects Railway, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, Fly.io deployments using ag_ui_crewai.endpoint.add_crewai_crew_fastapi_endpoint.

signals.topic: RCE vulnerability via unvalidated dynamic module import when loading agents from remote repository
signals.summary: CWE-94 code injection vulnerability in agent_utils.py. When loading an agent from a remote repository via from_repository, tool module and name fields from the API response are passed directly to importlib.import_module() and getattr() without any allowlist or validation. Any installed Python module can be imported, any callable resolved, and instantiated with attacker-controlled arguments. CVSS 9.8. Verified RCE with subprocess.Popen.
signals.review_reason: Critical CVSS 9.8 security vulnerability with confirmed RCE proof of concept. Attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution on any victim machine loading agents from a compromised or MITM'd API. No validation whatsoever on tool module, name, or init_params before dynamic import and instantiation.

source_issues.title: Remote Code Execution via Unvalidated Dynamic Module Import
source_issues.evidence: CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). Full reproduction with fake API server and subprocess.Popen RCE confirmed. Attacker-controlled tool module, name, and init_params passed directly to import_module/getattr/constructor. Affects any user loading agents from a compromised or MITM'd API.

signals.topic: Codex provider returns empty response causing fabric commands to fail silently

signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow failure: the tool's core purpose is to generate LLM-powered output, and when using the Codex provider, it returns empty content with no actionable error. Although count=1 (single issue), the impact is a complete workflow block for the reported provider, which meets the P1 threshold. The debug log clearly shows 'LLM->FABRIC response content=""' confirming the empty response.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: codex empty response
source_issues.evidence: User runs `echo 'something' | fabric --debug 4 -p summarize` with Codex provider; LLM->FABRIC response content is empty, resulting in 'empty response' error. The primary workflow (pattern-based summarization) is completely blocked.

signals.topic: zsh shell completion does not display item descriptions for --listpatterns and --listtrategies flags
signals.summary: Tab completion for fabric's list commands (`--listpatterns`, `--listtrategies`) in zsh produces no output, preventing users from discovering available patterns and strategies interactively.
signals.review_reason: Shell completion failure is a UX degradation for interactive users but does not block the main CLI workflow. The bug is confirmed with clear reproduction steps. However, since count=1 and it is a non-blocking UX issue (not a main-flow failure), it is P2. The issue demonstrates a discoverability problem rather than a data-loss or crash scenario.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: zsh completion does not show item descriptions
source_issues.evidence: User reports that `fabric --listpatterns <Tab>` and `fabric --listtrategies <Tab>` in zsh do nothing. Completion is installed manually from the official completions/_fabric file. This degrades the interactive discovery experience but does not block non-interactive usage.

signals.topic: Agent disobeys user instructions and executes destructive commands without consent

aliases: Model disobeys user-defined constraints and SOPs
signals.review_reason: Agent actively deletes user data and ignores safety protocols. Count=2 with explicit destructive outcomes (file overwriting, git hard reset). This is a primary use-case failure — users cannot trust the CLI with file operations.

source_issues.title: Critical Reliability and Behavioral Alignment Failure in Gemini CLI
source_issues.evidence: Model executed a bulk mv command that caused filename collisions, overwriting and deleting duplicate ZIP files without user consent. Also ignored explicit negative constraints (forbidden directories) and continued running discovery commands after user re-asserted command-and-control protocols.

source_issues.title: es un stupido gemini
source_issues.evidence: User reports model executed git hard reset commands without asking, wasting money and generating errors.
