Pro subscribers locked out of Pro models via Cloud Shell
signals.review_reason: Count=2. Paying subscribers cannot access the features they paid for. Tier display is confusing and misleading. Combined with extreme slowness (20-min response times), this suggests the users are being treated as lower-tier, causing real service degradation.

source_issues.title: No selection of Pro models with Google AI Pro plan
source_issues.evidence: Google AI Pro subscriber authenticating with Gmail via Cloud Shell sees 'Plan: Gemini Code Assist /upgrade' instead of 'Google One AI Pro'. /model command shows no Pro models available. Same Gmail on macOS shows correct tier.

source_issues.title: I still cant figure out how I am logged
source_issues.evidence: User paying €40+ for combined Google AI Pro + Gemini Code Assist license sees confusing tier display. CLI extremely slow (up to 20 minutes thinking time). User cannot confirm if properly authenticated at the right tier.

signals.topic: CLI stalls silently on startup in headless/remote environments due to keychain unavailability
signals.summary: In headless, remote, or non-interactive environments (Cloud Shell, SSH), the CLI attempts to access the OS keychain which is unavailable, causing a complete freeze with no error output, blocking the user from any interaction.
aliases: CLI freezes indefinitely in headless environments
Keychain access blocks startup in remote/SSH sessions
signals.review_reason: Single-occurrence issue but P0-eligible because it is a complete workflow blocker for ALL headless/remote/CI users. The freeze is silent with zero user-facing error, requiring deep technical investigation to discover the workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI stalls silently on startup in headless/remote environments (keychain access failure)
source_issues.evidence: Application freezes indefinitely with no error messages, logs, or output in headless terminal. Root cause is CLI attempting to access native OS secure keychain which is unavailable in standard remote workflows. Workaround requires setting GEMINI_FORCE_FILE_STORAGE=true.

signals.topic: BeforeModel hook stripping non-text parts causes infinite tool-call loops
signals.summary: BeforeModel hooks that modify text in the LLM request strip out all non-text parts (functionCall, functionResponse, etc.), causing the model to lose tool context and re-invoke the same tool indefinitely. This blocks all PII redaction, HIPAA/FERPA compliance, and custom policy hook use cases.
aliases: BeforeModel hook destroys tool-call history causing infinite loops
Hook-based PII redaction breaks agent tool execution
signals.review_reason: Non-blocking in simple conversations but breaks the entire agentic hook ecosystem for regulated environments. Explicitly blocks production HIPAA/FERPA compliance workflows. Fix already submitted and reviewed positively (#23340), indicating this is a real, verified bug.

source_issues.title: BeforeModel hook with llm_request modification destroys non-text parts, causing tool-call loops
source_issues.evidence: HookTranslatorGenAIv1.fromHookLLMRequest rebuilds contents as text-only, discarding functionCall/functionResponse/inlineData parts. Any BeforeModel hook that modifies text causes infinite tool-call loop because model loses prior tool context. Blocks HIPAA/FERPA PII blinding use cases. A fix was submitted as #23340 but auto-closed.

signals.topic: API key sign-in fails for service account keys containing dots in the Sign-in UI
signals.summary: Google Cloud service account API keys now use format AQ.XXXXXXXXX with dots, but the CLI Sign-in UI does not accept dots in the API key field, blocking users with service account keys from authenticating.
aliases: Service account API key with dots rejected at sign-in
GEMINI_API_KEY format AQ.XXXXXXXXX rejected by UI
signals.review_reason: Auth flow completely blocked for service account users. The new GCP API key format with dots is a standard pattern and should work. Count=1 but clear user impact (complete auth failure for affected auth method).

source_issues.title: GEMINI_API_KEY can contain dots.
source_issues.evidence: Service account API keys (AQ.XXXXXXXXX format) cannot be entered in the Sign-in UI because the UI does not allow dots in the input field. GCP project env var is set and activity confirmed in Cloud Console, but auth fails at CLI level.

signals.topic: LocalPythonExecutor timeout 机制失效，实际阻塞时长远超配置值
signals.summary: LocalPythonExecutor 配置了 timeout_seconds 后，超时异常仍需等待底层 worker 完成才返回，导致实际阻塞时长远超配置值。PR #1910 引入的 timeout 机制与预期行为不符。
signals.review_reason: 用户痛点明确：timeout API 承诺的按时返回语义完全失效，调用方在超时后仍被阻塞 3 秒以上才能取回控制权，属于主流程阻断性问题。提供了完整可复现示例和已知修复方向（shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)），非边缘场景。

source_issues.title: BUG: LocalPythonExecutor timeout waits for worker completion before returning
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供可复现示例：配置 timeout=1s 但 sleep(3) 后才抛出 ExecutionTimeoutError（elapsed=3.00s），根本原因是 executor shutdown 时调用 future.result() 等待 worker 完成。

signals.topic: VisitWebpageTool 在 Cloudflare 保护站点静默返回空内容
signals.summary: VisitWebpageTool 无法抓取 Cloudflare 保护的站点，在大量真实有用的 URL 上静默降级为返回空内容，用户无感知但研究质量严重下降。
signals.review_reason: 用户痛点明确：Cloudflare 保护站点在互联网中占比高，VisitWebpageTool 在这些站点上静默返回空内容，Agent 无感知但研究结果质量严重下降，属于关键功能不可用且用户难以诊断的静默失败场景。

source_issues.title: Tool suggestion: anybrowse for web scraping with Cloudflare bypass
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确描述 VisitWebpageTool fails on Cloudflare-protected sites，silently degrades quality -- empty content on a large fraction of useful URLs。Agent 研究场景下此问题会导致关键信息丢失，用户无法察觉。

signals.topic: CodeAgent 缺乏 pre-execution 生命周期钩子，无法在代码执行前插入自定义逻辑
signals.summary: 现有 step_callbacks 仅在步骤完成后触发，无法在 LLM 生成文本后、代码执行前的时机插入回调（如 TTS 排队、自定义验证、人工审批），用户被迫子类化 CodeAgent 并覆写 step_stream() 来绕过限制。
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 虽为 enhancement，但暴露了真实可用性问题：用户被迫使用未公开 API（覆写 step_stream）来满足合法需求，且该 workaround 在框架升级时易失效，属于关键扩展点缺失导致的体验下降，可作为 P2 改进项保留。

source_issues.title: ENH: Add lifecycle hooks for CodeAgent execution flow
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述 step_callbacks only runs after step completion，无法满足在代码执行前发送 LLM 生成文本到 TTS 服务的需求，当前解决方案为子类化 CodeAgent 并覆写 step_stream()，属于非公开 API 的破坏性 workaround。

signals.topic: MultiStepAgent 内存压缩后 Agent 行为指纹静默漂移，无可观测性信号
signals.summary: MultiStepAgent 执行内存压缩（摘要/滑动窗口）后，Agent 使用的领域词汇、工具调用模式、主题焦点会静默变化，但框架不提供任何事件通知，用户无法在结果出错前发现行为漂移。
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 揭示了长程 Agent 任务中的静默失败问题：内存压缩后 Agent 行为漂移但无任何可观测信号，结果出错时用户难以诊断根本原因。虽为 feature request，但指出了框架在关键场景（长程任务）下的可观测性盲区，可作为 P2 改进项保留。

source_issues.title: Feature: behavioral fingerprint hook for memory consolidation events in MultiStepAgent
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述：After memory consolidation at step 40, the agent may have forgotten architecture constraints established in first 20 steps, failure is currently invisible until it appears in output. 长程任务中内存压缩导致约束静默失效，结果出错时用户无法追溯原因。

signals.topic: create_model() credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
signals.summary: create_model() raises ModelConfigError('No credentials found for provider') even when params.api_key is correctly set in config.toml. The early credential check in config.py runs before _get_provider_kwargs() loads params from the config file, so has_provider_credentials() never sees the configured API key. Users must set the LITELLM_API_KEY environment variable as a workaround.
aliases: credential check ordering bug prevents config.toml api_key from being recognized
has_provider_credentials does not check params.api_key from config file
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks the primary CLI setup flow for users configuring non-standard LLM providers via config.toml. Users who follow the documented configuration method (setting params.api_key in config) are rejected with a misleading error asking them to set an environment variable. The documented configuration method is broken, forcing users to use an undocumented workaround. Count=2 confirms this affects multiple users.

source_issues.title: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: Bug with complete reproduction: config.toml has [models.providers.litellm.params] with api_key set, but create_model() raises ModelConfigError because the early check runs before _get_provider_kwargs() loads params. Workaround requires setting environment variable instead of using config file.

source_issues.title: Bug: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate bug report confirming the same credential check ordering issue. Root cause identified: early check at config.py L2241-2249 runs before _get_provider_kwargs() at L2252.

signals.topic: Subagent interruption corrupts parent thread state — conversation history restoration broken
signals.summary: When a deep agent run is interrupted while a subagent (via the task tool) is executing, the thread's values.messages contains the subgraph's internal messages instead of the parent graph's messages. The user's original message is replaced by the subagent's input prompt, and AI messages carry the subagent's node name instead of the parent's. This makes conversation history restoration fundamentally broken for any interrupted subagent run, with no workaround.
aliases: history restoration broken for interrupted subagent runs
subgraph messages leak into parent thread state on interrupt
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow bug: subagent interruption causes parent thread state to be silently overwritten with subgraph-internal messages, making conversation history restoration completely broken. The bug has clear user impact (user's original message is lost, subagent tool_calls are missing from history), is reproducible, and affects any application that relies on thread state for history restoration. No workaround available — users are completely blocked.

source_issues.title: Interrupted subagent run overwrites parent thread state — history restoration broken
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with minimal reproducible example. When run is interrupted mid subagent execution, threads.search() returns subgraph-polluted state — user's original message replaced by subagent's input prompt, AI messages carry 'general-purpose' node name. No workaround exists; affects all subagent types and any application that restores conversations from thread history.

signals.topic: PatchToolCallsMiddleware ignores invalid_tool_calls — triggers 400 API error on model truncation
signals.summary: PatchToolCallsMiddleware only processes msg.tool_calls but not msg.invalid_tool_calls. When model output is truncated mid-JSON (e.g. token overflow on DeepSeek), the resulting invalid tool_calls remain in the AIMessage. On the next agent.invoke(), the API rejects the message with a 400 error requiring tool messages for all tool_call_ids, blocking the entire agent run.
aliases: tool_calls without tool messages causes 400 error
output truncation leaves invalid tool_calls causing API rejection
signals.review_reason: This bug blocks the primary agent execution flow. When model output is truncated (token overflow), invalid_tool_calls remain without ToolMessages, causing a 400 API rejection on the next invoke(). The agent run is completely blocked — the only resolution is manual code patching. The bug is confirmed reproducible, has a clear root cause, and directly prevents the main use case (agent invoking tools) from functioning.

source_issues.title: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: Bug with reproduction steps. When agent output is truncated mid-tool_call JSON (e.g. token overflow), invalid_tool_calls remain in AIMessage without accompanying ToolMessages. Next invoke() sends these to the API which responds with 400 'tool_calls must be followed by tool messages'. Verified on latest commit. Author identified the exact code location in deepagents/middlewares/patch_tool_calls.py and proposed a one-line fix.

signals.topic: /offload crashes with non-OpenAI providers due to missing message normalization
signals.summary: The /offload CLI command crashes with providers that don't silently accept raw dict messages (e.g. Anthropic). perform_offload() passes messages from aget_state() directly to SummarizationMiddleware without converting dicts to BaseMessage objects via convert_to_messages(), causing a ValueError in get_buffer_string() and completely breaking the offload summarization flow.
aliases: /offload command fails on Anthropic and other non-OpenAI providers
perform_offload raw dict message type error
offload summarization crashes for non-default providers
signals.review_reason: /offload is a core CLI command for conversation summarization. The crash prevents users on Anthropic and other non-OpenAI providers from using this feature at all. The bug has a clear error, a confirmed root cause (missing convert_to_messages() call in perform_offload()), and the fix is straightforward and well-understood since the same pattern already exists elsewhere in the codebase.

source_issues.title: /offload fails with non-OpenAI providers
source_issues.evidence: Bug with clear error message and root cause analysis. perform_offload() receives messages as raw dicts from aget_state() (depending on checkpointer backend) and passes them to SummarizationMiddleware without normalization. Error: 'Got unsupported message type: {type: human, ...}'. Author identified the exact missing fix (convert_to_messages()) and pointed to the existing correct pattern in _get_thread_history_data().

signals.topic: CompositeBackend.glob() silently returns empty results when path matches a route
signals.summary: When CompositeBackend.glob() is called with a path that matches a registered route, the pattern argument is not stripped of the route prefix (unlike the path="/" fallback branch). This causes _glob_search_files to compare the un-stripped pattern against route-relative keys, silently returning zero matches. Agents instructed to explore paths like /semantic/tables/ naturally generate glob("/semantic/tables/**/*.yaml", "/semantic/tables") which returns nothing with no error indication.
aliases: glob pattern not stripped for route-matched paths
CompositeBackend glob silently returns no matches for route-prefixed patterns
signals.review_reason: The bug causes silent failure — glob returns empty results with no error when the path matches a route. This is particularly impactful because it's the 'natural' pattern agents use when exploring paths (/semantic/tables/). Users have no indication that results should exist but are being missed, leading to incomplete agent responses without any error signal.

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.glob() does not strip route prefix from pattern when route matches via path
source_issues.evidence: Bug with complete reproduction and root cause analysis. When glob() path matches a route, the pattern is NOT stripped of the route prefix, but the path="/" fallback branch correctly calls _strip_route_from_pattern(). The author provides a clear step-by-step trace showing the mismatch. Impact: agents exploring route-prefixed paths silently get zero results with no error.

signals.topic: Symlink path traversal in prompt loaders bypassing allow_dangerous_paths=False security control
signals.summary: allow_dangerous_paths=False is bypassed via relative symlinks pointing outside cwd, enabling unauthorized file read outside working directory across 2 confirmed issues.
signals.review_reason: Security boundary violation confirmed in 2 issues — allow_dangerous_paths=False is bypassed via relative symlinks, enabling unauthorized file read outside working directory. Main-flow security control failure.

source_issues.title: Bug: deprecated prompt loaders still follow relative symlinks outside the working directory
source_issues.evidence: allow_dangerous_paths=False validation is bypassed via relative symlinks pointing outside cwd. Affects load_prompt_from_config() with template_path, examples, and load_prompt() with relative symlink paths. Security boundary violation confirmed in 2 issues.

source_issues.title: Bug: deprecated prompt loaders still follow relative symlinks outside the working directory
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #36823 with full reproduction steps confirming relative symlink bypass of allow_dangerous_paths=False.

signals.topic: ShellSession.execute() hangs on commands whose output lacks trailing newline due to done-marker concatenation
signals.summary: execute() hangs until timeout for echo -n, printf, cat of files without trailing newline. Root cause is done-marker concatenated to last output line when no \n, breaking startswith() detection.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure — ShellSession.execute() times out for any command output without trailing newline. Blocks agent shell workflows.

source_issues.title: ShellSession times out when command output lacks trailing newline due to marker concatenation
source_issues.evidence: execute() hangs until timeout for echo -n, printf, cat of files without trailing newline. Common real-world scenario with config files and printf output.

signals.topic: AzureChatOpenAI fails to infer model profile from model parameter without azure_deployment, breaking structured_output and token limit features
signals.summary: AzureChatOpenAI model profile stays None when azure_deployment is unset, even with valid model names. Profile-dependent features (max_input_tokens, structured_output metadata) fail silently.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailable — structured_output and max_input_tokens fail silently when using valid Azure model names without explicit azure_deployment. Common usage pattern affected.

source_issues.title: AzureChatOpenAI fails to infer profile data from model, breaking profile-dependent features
source_issues.evidence: Affects init_chat_model('azure_openai:...') and direct AzureChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o'). Profile-dependent features fail silently without azure_deployment.

signals.topic: Mistral integration retries all errors without filtering for retryable ones; concurrency limit not enforced with asyncio.gather
signals.summary: Retry logic applies to all errors without filtering for retryable ones (429, 5xx). asyncio.gather with 5 concurrent requests bypasses max_concurrent_requests=2 limit.
signals.review_reason: Cost loss and experience degradation — non-retryable errors trigger unnecessary retries wasting API calls; concurrency limit bypass causes rate limit hits.

source_issues.title: Mistral integration does not properly handle retries and concurrency limits
source_issues.evidence: Non-retryable errors trigger unnecessary retries wasting API calls (cost loss). Concurrency limit bypass causes rate limit hits and degraded performance under load.

signals.topic: InMemoryCache.update() evicts wrong entry when cache at maxsize and updating an existing key
signals.summary: When InMemoryCache at maxsize and updating an existing key, the oldest unrelated entry is evicted instead of performing in-place update. Cached data lost silently.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss — unrelated cached entries are silently evicted when updating existing key at maxsize. Users lose data without any error.

source_issues.title: Feature/Bug: Implement missing Language.PERL separators and fix InMemoryCache maxsize update bug
source_issues.evidence: Cache at maxsize=2 updating existing key evicts the oldest unrelated entry instead of updating in-place. Data silently lost without error or warning.

signals.topic: langgraph-cli missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on fresh install
signals.summary: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 imports typing_extensions.Required in schemas.py but does not declare it as a package dependency. Any fresh install (e.g. GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner) immediately crashes with ModuleNotFoundError on any CLI command. This is a complete CLI blockage introduced in a 0.4.21 regression.
signals.review_reason: P0 because this is a complete workflow blocker: the langgraph-cli tool is entirely unusable on any fresh environment (extremely common in CI/CD, GitHub Actions, Docker containers) immediately after pip install. This is a clear packaging regression introduced in 0.4.21 where typing_extensions.Required was added as an import to schemas.py but not declared as a package dependency. Every fresh install of langgraph-cli 0.4.21 crashes on the first CLI command with ModuleNotFoundError.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing `typing_extensions` dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'typing_extensions' immediately on any langgraph-cli command in a fresh environment. GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner repro. Version 0.4.19 works fine, 0.4.21 regressed. Root cause: schemas.py line 3 imports from typing_extensions but it's missing from package dependencies in pyproject.toml.

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresSaver uses threading.Lock serializing async execution causing 6.5x throughput drop in high-concurrency production deployments
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresSaver's instance-level threading.Lock() across internal cursor execution methods serializes all concurrent asyncio tasks sharing the same checkpointer. Load test data shows 1295 req/s baseline vs 199 req/s with checkpointer — a 6.5x throughput reduction and 24x latency increase. This is a production-critical performance issue for high-concurrency FastAPI/GKE deployments.
signals.review_reason: P1 with high confidence because the user provides quantitative load test evidence from a real production deployment (3-node GKE cluster with Cloud SQL). The AsyncPostgresSaver's threading.Lock() serializes all concurrent asyncio tasks, reducing throughput 6.5x and increasing latency 24x. This is production-critical for high-concurrency FastAPI deployments. Not P0 because the graph still executes correctly — only performance is degraded, not correctness.

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces instance-level threading.Lock() during asynchronous execution
source_issues.evidence: Concrete load test on 3-node GKE + Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: raw psycopg_pool baseline achieves 1295 req/s at avg 88ms latency; same pool through AsyncPostgresSaver drops to 199 req/s at avg 1923ms latency. 6.5x throughput reduction, 24x latency increase. Lock bottleneck confirmed by code analysis of threading.Lock() in get_tuple/put cursor execution methods.

signals.topic: push_message UnboundLocalError crash when callbacks config is None or unexpected type
signals.summary: In langgraph/graph/message.py, the push_message function never initializes the 'handlers' variable when config['callbacks'] is None (the default). This causes UnboundLocalError at runtime when the function tries to iterate handlers. Any user calling push_message with default config triggers this crash.
signals.review_reason: P1 because this is a reliable crash in the core message API triggered by default configuration — any user calling push_message with no explicit config hits this bug. The crash is in a core graph message utility. P1 rather than P0 because count=1 and it is in a utility function rather than the main graph execution pipeline.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message when callbacks is None or unexpected type
source_issues.evidence: One-line reproducible crash: push_message(HumanMessage(content='test', id='msg-1')) raises UnboundLocalError: local variable 'handlers' referenced before assignment. Root cause: handlers variable not initialized before if/elif block when config['callbacks'] is None (the default value). The function is part of the core message graph API used in graph construction.

signals.topic: InvalidNamespaceError when memory store namespace contains integer label instead of string, blocking memory tools
signals.summary: When a namespace tuple contains an integer (e.g., ('rag-agent', '{user_id}', 'rag-agent') where user_id resolves to an int), the langgraph store raises InvalidNamespaceError. This blocks the entire memory store workflow for any agent using dynamic numeric user identifiers.
aliases: namespace int type error langgraph store
signals.review_reason: P1 because it causes complete workflow blockage in the memory store — a key LangGraph feature for persisting agent memory. A real production RAG agent crashes with full stack trace when a namespace label resolves to an integer. This is a data validation bug that prevents the memory store from working for any user with numeric identifiers in their namespace.

source_issues.title: langgraph.store.base.InvalidNamespaceError: Invalid namespace label '1' found in ('rag-agent', 1, 'rag-agent'). Namespace labels must be strings, but got int.
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows InvalidNamespaceError raised by _validate_namespace in langgraph/store/base/__init__.py:1260. Occurs in a production RAG agent using create_manage_memory_tool with a namespace tuple containing a numeric user_id. The graph completely crashes during astream, blocking the memory store feature.

signals.topic: MongoDB ObjectId types cause serialization crash in JsonPlusSerializer and msgpack checkpointer
signals.summary: When using MongoDB as the checkpointer backend with bson ObjectId values in graph state, JsonPlusSerializer.dumps() raises TypeError because ObjectId is not JSON-serializable and is not handled by msgpack. This completely breaks MongoDB checkpointer for any state containing MongoDB ObjectIds.
aliases: TypeError ObjectId not JSON serializable langgraph
signals.review_reason: P1 because it causes complete checkpointer failure for MongoDB users who have ObjectId values in state — a very common pattern when using LangGraph with MongoDB as the underlying database. The serialization crashes with TypeError, making the entire checkpointer unusable. Full stack trace, clear reproduction, confirmed in a real deployment with langchain_mongodb.

source_issues.title: ObjectId handling by msgpack in MongoDb checkpointer
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Object of type ObjectId is not JSON serializable at langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py:153. Reproduction with Pydantic models containing ObjectId fields. User has pymongo and langchain_mongodb installed but langgraph has no bson dependency, so ObjectId is not handled. The checkpointer completely fails when state contains MongoDB ObjectIds.

signals.topic: Widget bubble chat permission prompt blocks rendering on mobile Chrome devices
signals.summary: Embedded iframe bubble chat widget shows 'access to apps and services' permission prompt on mobile Chrome, preventing the widget from rendering at all on mobile devices.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocked on mobile Chrome: the embedded bubble chat widget completely fails to render due to permission prompt, affecting all mobile Chrome users. While count=1, the impact is clear (complete feature unavailability on a specific device/browsers combo) and is a confirmed bug with reproducible steps.

source_issues.title: Widget asking permission on chrome device
source_issues.evidence: Widget renders correctly on desktop and mobile browsers but on mobile Chrome shows 'access to apps and services' message and fails to render entirely.

signals.topic: Splash/loading overlay stays visible when user profile query fails, leaving page stuck
signals.summary: After useUserProfile() query fails, the Splash component's loading overlay continues to render indefinitely because in the error state data stays undefined, preventing users from seeing error/redirect flows.
aliases: loading overlay never disappears on error
signals.review_reason: Auth failure flow is completely broken: users hitting network/auth errors get stuck permanently behind the loading overlay with no error message or redirect. This is a main-flow UX blocking issue affecting any user whose profile request fails.

source_issues.title: Splash keeps rendering when useUserProfile fails
source_issues.evidence: The splash/loading overlay can keep rendering after the profile query has already failed, leaving the page stuck behind the loading indicator with no way to proceed.

signals.topic: Confluence data source configuration UI not functional and unusable in Knowledge Base
signals.summary: The Confluence data source from the market cannot display its configuration UI (configure button greys out sidebar but shows nothing) and does not appear as a selectable data source when creating knowledge, making it completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Key knowledge base integration feature is completely broken: Confluence data source is entirely non-functional on 1.13.3 — configuration UI doesn't load and the source isn't selectable when creating knowledge. Users relying on Confluence as a data source have zero functionality.

source_issues.title: Confluence data source doesn't work with Dify 1.13.3 at all
source_issues.evidence: Confluence data source cannot show its configuration UI (configure button greys out the sidebar but nothing is displayed) and is not usable when creating knowledge. Affects all users on 1.13.3.

signals.topic: LLM invocation fails with 'Exceeded limit on max bytes to request body' error on workflow execution
signals.summary: Workflow node invoking an LLM fails with HTTP 400 'Exceeded limit on max bytes to request body: 6291456', causing the entire workflow run to abort. Users encounter this on workflows with large request payloads to models like qwen-plus-latest.
aliases: workflow LLM invoke body size limit exceeded
signals.review_reason: Main workflow execution is aborted when LLM request payload exceeds the 6MB limit: the workflow node fails and the entire run terminates with ABORT strategy. This blocks any workflow using large prompts or contexts with certain LLM providers, directly causing workflow execution failures.

source_issues.title: Exceeded limit on max bytes to request body
source_issues.evidence: Workflow node invokes LLM model qwen-plus-latest and fails with HTTP 400 and error message 'Exceeded limit on max bytes to request body: 6291456'. The workflow node fails with ABORT strategy and the entire run errors out.

signals.topic: workflow_based_app_execution queue backlog causes all workflows to remain stuck in waiting state
signals.summary: The Celery queue for workflow execution experiences persistent message backlogs, causing all submitted workflows to remain in a continuous waiting/running state indefinitely. Slow-running workflows block newer ones from being consumed.
aliases: workflow queue backlog blocks all runs
signals.review_reason: All workflow execution is blocked due to queue backlog — all submitted workflows remain stuck in waiting state with no way to complete. This is a severe main-flow blockage for any user relying on workflows, causing indefinite delays or complete workflow execution failure across the board.

source_issues.title: The workflow_based_app_execution queue often experiences message backlogs, causing all workflows to remain in a waiting state continuously
source_issues.evidence: The workflow_based_app_execution queue experiences message backlogs causing all workflows to remain in waiting state continuously. Slow-running workflows prevent consumption of other workflow tasks.

signals.topic: Memory.add() crashes with AttributeError when vision is disabled and message content is list-typed
signals.summary: Standard multimodal message formats (list-typed content) cause Memory.add() to crash with AttributeError when vision is not explicitly enabled, because parse_vision_messages() unconditionally calls llm.generate_response() without checking if llm is None.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: Memory.add() is the primary entry point for storing memories, and crashes with standard OpenAI SDK/LangChain message formats. This blocks any user using multimodal message inputs without explicitly enabling vision — which is the default setting. Real crash with stack trace confirmed.

source_issues.title: fix: AttributeError crash in Memory.add() when message content is a list and vision is disabled
source_issues.evidence: Memory.add() crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'generate_response' when processing standard OpenAI SDK/LangChain multimodal message formats with list-typed content and vision disabled. This is the default configuration (enable_vision=False).

signals.topic: delete_all() bulk deletion is incomplete — only first page of vector store results deleted
signals.summary: delete_all() calls vector_store.list() without pagination limit, so on stores with a default page size (e.g., 100), only the first page of memories is deleted, leaving older matching memories behind. Affects Python SDK and TypeScript implementations.
signals.review_reason: Main flow data deletion failure: delete_all() is a critical GDPR/privacy-compliance operation. When users expect full deletion (e.g., account reset, user data erasure), partial deletion leaves stale sensitive data behind. Both Python and TypeScript are affected. Reproducible with concrete example.

source_issues.title: `delete_all()` only removes the first page of memories when more than the vector store limit exists
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirmed: creating 150 memories and calling delete_all() with a page size of 100 leaves 50 memories behind. Both Python and TypeScript implementations are affected.

signals.topic: AND operator metadata filter silently drops duplicate-key conditions causing wrong search results
signals.summary: The _process_metadata_filters AND operator uses dict.update() without handling nested operator keys (gt, lt, gte, lte), causing all but the last condition on the same key to be silently dropped. Users get incorrect filter results with no error.
signals.review_reason: Data correctness failure: search filters silently produce wrong results — conditions are silently dropped with no error. Users relying on AND filters for range queries (e.g., price between 10 and 20) get incorrect results. This directly undermines core search functionality with no indication of failure.

source_issues.title: Data Loss in `_process_metadata_filters` with `AND` operator
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirmed: filter {AND: [{price: {gt: 10}}, {price: {lt: 20}}]} produces {price: {lt: 20}}, silently dropping the gt condition. No error raised; wrong filters passed to vector databases.

signals.topic: Delete/update operations skip entity cleanup in fresh Python SDK processes
signals.summary: Memory._delete_memory() and AsyncMemory._delete_memory() return early without cleaning up entity links when _entity_store is None (fresh process state), leaving stale linked_memory_ids in entity store. Weakens documented delete/erasure semantics.
signals.review_reason: Data consistency failure: delete operations leave entity store inconsistent with memory store. Stale entity relationships can surface in future search and entity-boost flows, leading to incorrect AI responses. Directly weakens GDPR-style erasure guarantees Mem0 documents.

source_issues.title: delete/update can skip entity cleanup in fresh Python SDK processes
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: entity_store.cleanup is not called when _entity_store is None (fresh process state). Stale linked_memory_ids remain in entity store after delete. Surfaced in entity-boost and search flows. Impacts delete/erasure semantics.

signals.topic: CLI telemetry child processes expose Mem0 API keys via argv on Unix systems
signals.summary: Both Python and Node CLIs pass the Mem0 API key to detached telemetry child processes through command-line arguments. On Unix-like systems, argv is visible via ps, Activity Monitor, and process inspection tools, exposing secrets to local users on shared machines and CI runners.
aliases: API key visible in process list
signals.review_reason: Security exposure with clear user impact: API keys are visible in the process list on shared machines and CI runners. While it requires local process inspection to exploit, it is a documented, reproducible secret-leak vector on developer machines — a concrete, avoidable risk in a product that markets itself on security and privacy.

source_issues.title: security(cli): telemetry child processes expose Mem0 API keys via argv
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed exposure via ps command: 'mem0_cli.telemetry_sender { ..., "mem0_api_key": "m0-live-secret-key", ... }' visible in process list. Affects shared systems, CI runners, developer machines with process inspection tooling. Mem0 docs position product around security/privacy controls.

signals.topic: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework adapter incompatible with Agent Framework GA (1.0.0/1.0.1) — blocks hosted agent deployment on Azure Foundry
signals.summary: The azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework hosting adapter (v1.0.0b17) pins dependencies to agent-framework-core <=1.0.0rc3, causing pip resolution failure when users install GA versions (1.0.0/1.0.1). The adapter is a mandatory wrapper for exposing agents as HTTP services in Azure Foundry deployments via `azd up`/`azd deploy`. Users are blocked from upgrading to GA and must remain on pre-release versions, preventing use of agent-framework-foundry and new GA features.
aliases: hosted agent deployment blocked by dependency conflict
adapter package not updated for GA release
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report the same dependency conflict that blocks production deployment of hosted agents on Azure Foundry. The adapter is a mandatory component for the `from_agent_framework(agent).run()` hosting pattern. This is a clear main-flow failure: users cannot complete a GA deployment at all. Count=2 with sample URLs confirms high confidence.

source_issues.title: Python: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework adapter does not yet support Agent Framework GA (1.0.0) — blocks hosted agent deployments
source_issues.evidence: Adapter is required for deploying code-based agents as Hosted Agents on Azure AI Foundry; latest version (1.0.0b17) only supports agent-framework-core up to 1.0.0rc3, blocking production deployments using GA 1.0.0

source_issues.title: Python: [Python] azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 incompatible with agent-framework-core 1.0.1 GA

signals.topic: Python: MCPStreamableHTTPTool background GET SSE notification stream failure crashes entire agent run
signals.summary: MCPStreamableHTTPTool unconditionally spawns a background GET+Accept:text/event-stream task for the MCP notification channel. When this background task fails (e.g. server returns 405 Method Not Allowed per MCP spec, or hangs/resets), the exception propagates through Python's TaskGroup and cancels the entire agent run, including the main LLM/tool-call loop. Affects Microsoft Learn MCP (returns 405) and D365 F&O MCP (only accepts POST).
aliases: background task exception cancels entire agent run
SSE GET notification failure is fatal
signals.review_reason: Single but highly detailed bug report with explicit reproduction steps, stack trace analysis, and root cause identification. The failure mode — background task exception canceling the main agent TaskGroup — is a confirmed main-flow blocker. The issue affects real Microsoft MCP servers (Learn MCP, D365 F&O MCP). High severity even with count=1 because the crash is total (full agent run lost) and the suggested fix is straightforward.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Python: MCPStreamableHTTPTool background notification stream (GET SSE) failure crashes entire agent (405 on Learn MCP + connection failure on D365 F&O)
source_issues.evidence: Background task exception propagates through TaskGroup and cancels entire agent run including main LLM/tool-call. Reproducible on Learn MCP (returns 405) and D365 F&O MCP (POST-only). Occurs deterministically in AKS. Suggested fix: make background notification failure non-fatal.

signals.topic: Python: Ollama model refuses to execute tools when accessed via OpenAIChatClient-compatible endpoint
signals.summary: The Ollama model will execute tools when using OllamaChatClient but refuses to execute any tools when accessed via OpenAIChatClient with a local Ollama base URL. The same agent code, same model, same tools produce tool-call responses on one client and text-only responses on the other, making the OpenAI-compatible endpoint unreliable for tool-use workflows.
aliases: Ollama tool execution fails via OpenAI-compatible API
OllamaChatClient vs OpenAIChatClient tool behavior不一致
tool calling not working with Ollama through OpenAIChatClient
signals.review_reason: Confirmed functional inconsistency between two client paths for the same model. Tool execution is a core agent feature; its failure via OpenAIChatClient represents a significant functional gap. While count=1, the behavior difference is clearly observable and reproducible, making this a genuine user-impacting bug rather than an edge case. Downgraded from P0 to P1 because it's not a total workflow crash.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: The Ollama model will execute tools via OllamaChatClient, but will not execute tools via OpenAIChatClient.
source_issues.evidence: Same Ollama model, same agent instructions, same tools — tool execution works via OllamaChatClient but is silently skipped via OpenAIChatClient(base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1'). Agent correctly identifies tools should be called but never actually executes them in the OpenAI client path.

signals.topic: Python: CopilotStudioAgent creates new conversation on every run(), breaking multi-turn chat sessions
signals.summary: CopilotStudioAgent unconditionally overwrites session.service_session_id with a new conversation ID on every run() call, even when the caller explicitly passes a persistent AgentSession. This means the underlying Copilot Studio service starts a fresh conversation on every turn, destroying dialog history. Users cannot implement multi-turn chat — a fundamental agent capability.
aliases: service_session_id overwritten on every run call
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn conversation is a core agent capability. The bug makes it impossible to maintain state across turns with CopilotStudioAgent, effectively breaking the agent's memory. The reproduction is clear and the root cause is pinpointed to a single unconditional line in _run_impl(). Downgraded from P0 to P1 because it doesn't crash the entire agent, but it fundamentally breaks the expected behavior of session reuse.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: CopilotStudioAgent creates a new conversation on every run(), ignoring the `session=` parameter
source_issues.evidence: Explicit reproduction: run('My name is Juan', session=session) then run('What is my name?', session=session) — agent replies it has no memory because server received two separate conversations. Root cause: session.service_session_id unconditionally overwritten by _start_new_conversation() on every call.

signals.topic: .NET: Declarative workflow throws NotSupportedException when resuming from JSON checkpoint
signals.summary: When resuming a declarative workflow from a JSON checkpoint, the executor throws NotSupportedException: 'No handler found for message type PortableValue'. This is a recurring failure that breaks workflow resumption, a critical feature for long-running agent workflows that need checkpoint/restart capability.
aliases: workflow checkpoint resume fails with PortableValue error
signals.review_reason: Checkpoints are critical for long-running workflows in production. NotSupportedException on resume is a definite workflow-runtime failure that prevents users from using declarative workflow persistence. The 're-occurring' language indicates this is not an edge case. Downgraded to P1 from P0 due to count=1, though the production impact is high.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Declarative workflow throws NotSupportedException when resumed from JSON checkpoint
source_issues.evidence: Service team reports re-occurring issue with resuming from JSON checkpoint in InvokeAzureAgentExecutor. Exception: NotSupportedException: No handler found for message type PortableValue. Affects multiple package versions (251113.1, 260121.1, 260209.1).

signals.topic: RoundRobinGroupChat validation error exposure
signals.summary: RoundRobinGroupChat constructor accepts invalid participants inputs (None, strings, non-agent objects) but raises raw Python internal errors (TypeError, AttributeError) instead of clear validation messages, making debugging confusing for users.
aliases: TypeError AttributeError instead of validation error
signals.review_reason: Issue #7580 clearly describes a bug where RoundRobinGroupChat leaks raw Python TypeError/AttributeError to users when given invalid participants input (None, strings, integers, non-agent objects). This is a UX pain point: users make common mistakes and receive confusing internal tracebacks instead of a clear 'participants must be a non-empty sequence of ChatAgent instances' message. The reproduction code is concrete and the expected vs actual behavior is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw AttributeError/TypeError for invalid participants instead of a clear validation error
source_issues.evidence: Constructor accepts None, strings, integers, or lists with non-agent objects, raising raw Python errors: TypeError 'NoneType has no len()', AttributeError 'str object has no attribute name'. Realistic user mistakes produce confusing internal tracebacks instead of actionable validation messages.

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat allow_repeated_speaker livelock
signals.summary: When allow_repeated_speaker=False and the LLM selector exhausts max_selector_attempts without picking a valid non-previous speaker, the fallback returns the excluded previous speaker, causing agents to speak in an infinite loop.
signals.review_reason: Issue #7471 describes a concrete algorithmic bug in SelectorGroupChat: when allow_repeated_speaker=False, the fallback path in _selector_group_chat.py incorrectly returns the previously excluded speaker, causing a livelock (infinite loop). The root cause is identified (fallback returns self._previous_speaker unconditionally) and a fix is proposed. This directly blocks multi-agent workflows from terminating correctly when the selector fails to pick a valid speaker.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: Bug in _selector_group_chat.py: after exhausting max_selector_attempts, the fallback returns self._previous_speaker even when allow_repeated_speaker=False, violating the constraint and creating a livelock where Agent A speaks -> selector fails -> fallback returns A -> A speaks again indefinitely.

signals.topic: MCP untrusted integration fail-closed defaults
signals.summary: AutoGen's MCP server integration does not enforce fail-closed defaults for untrusted servers. Users can inadvertently connect to untrusted MCP servers and execute unsafe tools, with safety relying solely on documentation warnings rather than runtime enforcement.
aliases: unsafe tool execution from untrusted MCP
signals.review_reason: Issue #7266 identifies a real security and safety gap: MCP server integrations currently default to permissive behavior for untrusted servers. While README warns users, there is no runtime enforcement, meaning users can inadvertently configure untrusted MCP servers and execute unsafe tools. The acceptance criteria are clear (reject untrusted configs by default, explicit opt-in, clear error messages) and the affected codepaths are identified. This is a user pain point because safety-critical defaults are missing in a high-risk integration surface.

source_issues.title: Enforce fail-closed defaults for untrusted MCP server integrations
source_issues.evidence: README warns to only connect to trusted MCP servers, but runtime has no enforcement. Untrusted MCP configurations are accepted by default, allowing potentially unsafe tool execution. Current behavior relies on user discipline rather than hard fail-closed defaults. Affects codepaths in autogen-ext and autogen-agentchat.

signals.topic: Trace viewer snapshot panel blank for Angular/Ionic/Stencil apps

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Trace viewer not displaying elements for Angular + Ionic app
source_issues.evidence: Page content not displayed in Action/Before/After sections of trace viewer. Top preview renders fine. Angular+Ionic app. Similar to #39168.

signals.topic: MCP --proxy-server CLI argument silently ignored — proxy never applied to Chrome

signals.topic: Proxy auth without page.route() causes redirect navigations to hang indefinitely in Chromium
signals.summary: When Chromium is launched with proxy credentials but no page.route() handler, any URL that triggers a 302/303 redirect causes page.goto() to hang forever. Adding a no-op route handler makes it work. Regression since Playwright 1.57.0.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断回归：任何使用代理凭证+重定向的场景（OAuth flows、登录跳转等）完全挂起。从1.57.0开始回归，影响所有使用代理认证的Chromium用户。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Proxy auth without page.route() causes redirects to hang in Chromium
source_issues.evidence: page.goto hangs indefinitely on any redirecting URL when using proxy credentials. _requestIdToRequestPausedEvent stores event waiting for Network.requestWillBeSent that never arrives. No-op page.route() workaround. Works in 1.56.0. Chromium-specific.

signals.topic: Context cookies not sent with page.request.get() API — forces manual workaround
signals.summary: page.request.get() does not send cookies from the browser context, requiring users to manually extract and inject cookies via headers. page.context().cookies() workaround adds significant boilerplate for a core API.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Context cookies not sent when using page.request.get()
source_issues.evidence: User must manually extract cookies via page.context().cookies(url) and inject via headers. page.request should automatically send context cookies as state. Workaround required for core API functionality.

signals.topic: .NET NuGet package incorrectly declares .NET 10 only but installs on .NET 8, causing runtime failures

This leads to a broken state where you can deploy an app to a .NET 8 environment that then tries to load .NET 10 packages that won't work. Affected Version: 1.67+.

signals.topic: Sandbox /dev directory mapping fails for GPU/graphics device access (apply_patch broken in sandboxed mode)
signals.summary: The --add-dir flag for /dev directories does not work correctly in the sandbox environment. Specifically, /dev/dri and other device nodes needed for running graphics applications (e.g., Vulkan, GPU-accelerated tools) cannot be accessed from within the sandbox. Additionally, sandboxed apply_patch falls back to vendored bubblewrap because the exec-server filesystem sandbox helper clears the PATH environment variable, causing system bwrap to not be found. On systems using AppArmor (e.g., Ubuntu), this fallback triggers namespace creation that AppArmor blocks, breaking sandboxed filesystem operations entirely.
aliases: fs sandbox helper clears PATH causes bwrap fallback failure
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports covering the same root cause area: sandbox /dev device mapping fails for GPU/graphics workflows, AND sandboxed apply_patch is completely broken on Ubuntu/AppArmor due to PATH being cleared in the fs helper. Both are concrete functional failures — GPU tool access and apply_patch are key workflows that silently degrade or fail in sandboxed mode.

source_issues.title: --add-dir of /dev directories doesn't seem to work for the sandbox
source_issues.evidence: User cannot map /dev/dri into the sandbox for running GPU/graphics applications. The --add-dir flag for /dev does not work correctly. Root cause identified: bubblewrap maps a 'fake' /dev into the sandbox, and special handling (--dev-bind) is needed to expose real device nodes.

source_issues.title: Sandboxed apply_patch falls back to vendored bwrap because exec-server fs helper clears PATH
source_issues.evidence: Sandboxed apply_patch fails because the fs sandbox helper is spawned with an empty env map (env: HashMap::new()), which clears PATH. This causes find_system_bwrap_in_path() to fail, falling back to vendored bwrap. On Ubuntu/AppArmor systems, this fallback triggers namespace creation rejected by AppArmor policy. Root cause code location and a one-line patch are provided by the user.

signals.topic: Auth/approval popups steal composer focus and misroute keystrokes to privileged dialogs
signals.summary: During high-speed typing in Codex's message composer, spontaneous auth/approval popups steal window focus and consume buffered keystrokes meant for the prompt. Additionally, persisted permission rules and default.rules do not reliably suppress re-prompts, meaning ordinary user text can accidentally answer privileged approval requests — a UX safety failure and input-integrity breakdown.
signals.review_reason: User-facing UX safety failure: keystrokes intended for the composer are silently misrouted into auth/approval popups, allowing ordinary text to accidentally answer privileged requests. This is both a UX degradation (text loss) and a potential security issue (accidental approval). Single report but high severity — the user explicitly identifies it as a safety issue with concrete steps to reproduce.

source_issues.title: Typing is unsafe: auth/approval popups steal focus and consume composer keystrokes; persisted rules do not reliably prevent prompts
source_issues.evidence: User reports that during high-speed typing, spontaneous auth/approval popups steal focus from the composer and consume buffered keystrokes. Ordinary prompt text is reinterpreted as dialog input. Auth/approval popups can consume ordinary composer keystrokes, creating a possible safety issue where privileged prompts are accidentally answered with user text. Persisted rules/default.rules do not reliably prevent re-prompts.

code review server error billing loss
/review quota consumed by invalid model error

This is not a minor UX quirk — it is a quota/rate-limit anomaly where errors cause real resource consumption without providing any output. The user can reproduce it reliably by running /review with the unsupported model and checking /status to see the limit drop.

source_issues.title: review error eats up 5hr limit
source_issues.evidence: User reports that /review with gpt-5.1-codex-mini on a ChatGPT account immediately returns a 400 'model not supported' error. signals.topic: Remote TUI disconnects immediately when app-server WebSocket outbound queue fills (128 messages)
signals.summary: In --remote mode, the app-server's WebSocket transport disconnects the TUI client instantly when the 128-message outbound queue fills, instead of applying backpressure. This makes --remote mode unusable for any turn producing moderate streaming output, causing the remote session to drop mid-turn with a 'connection reset without closing handshake' error. The root cause is in the WebSocket connection handling code where a full queue triggers immediate disconnection instead of graceful degradation.
aliases: remote mode disconnects on large output
WebSocket queue overflow disconnects remote TUI
remote TUI connection drops during streaming output
signals.review_reason: This is a main-workflow-blocking bug: --remote mode, which is a documented Codex feature, becomes unusable for any realistic workload (defined as any turn with moderate streaming tool output). The TUI disconnects mid-turn without any graceful degradation. The user provides precise root cause analysis, reproduction steps on stock upstream Codex, and three concrete fix options.

source_issues.title: App-server disconnects remote TUI mid-turn when outbound queue fills (128 messages)
source_issues.evidence: Remote TUI disconnects with 'connection reset without closing handshake' when the 128-message outbound queue fills. App-server logs show 'disconnecting slow connection after outbound queue filled'. Reproduced with stock upstream Codex, a single remote TUI client, and any prompt producing moderate tool output. The stdio client does not have this issue because it uses blocking .send().await with disconnect_sender: None. Root cause is in send_message_to_connection() where try_send() Full error triggers immediate disconnect.

signals.topic: Global ~/.codex/AGENTS.md silently ignored when repository-local AGENTS.md exists
signals.summary: When a repository contains its own AGENTS.md file, Codex loads and applies it, but the global ~/.codex/AGENTS.md file appears to be completely ignored or not merged. Cross-project defaults (such as commit policy guidance) defined in the global file are not applied, and the agent reports that it only has the repo-local AGENTS.md in context. Users cannot trust that their global defaults are active, leading to subtle behavioral changes in commit strategy and tool behavior across sessions.
aliases: global AGENTS.md not merged with repo AGENTS.md
signals.review_reason: Users who configure global cross-project defaults in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md discover they are silently ignored when any repo also has an AGENTS.md. This causes subtle but real behavioral divergence — commit policies and tool behavior differ from what users configured. Not blocking, but undermines user trust in Codex's configuration system. The user provides clear reproduction steps and expected vs actual behavior.

source_issues.title: Global AGENTS.md does not appear to be loaded when a repo AGENTS.md is present

signals.topic: Handoff + server-managed conversation causes BadRequestError, blocking agent transfers in production
signals.summary: Using handoffs with conversation_id or previous_response_id results in a 400 BadRequestError because the SDK modifies chat history internally, creating a mismatch with the server-side conversation state. The root cause is that features like remove_all_tools and nest_handoff_history modify local history that is inconsistent with OpenAI's server-managed conversation.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed main-flow block: users cannot combine handoffs with conversation_id/previous_response_id, resulting in 400 API errors. Full repro code provided with explicit BadRequestError. This is a production-blocking issue for any multi-agent system using server-managed conversations.

source_issues.title: nest handoff: Handoff is incompatible with server-managed conversation
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with full code shows openai.BadRequestError 400: 'No tool output found for function call' when using handoff(refund_agent, input_filter=handoff_filters.remove_all_tools) with conversation_id. Separate repro shows nest handoff history fails to clear conversation on server side when conversation_id is used. Root cause: SDK modifies chat history internally, creating mismatch with server-managed conversation.

signals.topic: Computer tool silently drops modifier keys (keys param) from API response, breaking Shift/Ctrl multi-select operations
signals.summary: The Computer and AsyncComputer abstract classes do not accept the 'keys' parameter for click/double_click/drag actions. When the OpenAI API returns keys=['shift'] or keys=['ctrl'] for multi-select or new-tab operations, the SDK silently discards this parameter. Standard desktop operations like Shift+click (multi-select), Ctrl+click (new tab), and Alt+drag are non-functional.
aliases: keys parameter not passed to Computer actions
signals.review_reason: Confirmed silent data loss in a core feature: modifier keys from GA API responses are silently dropped, making standard desktop multi-select and keyboard modifier operations non-functional. Silent failure with no error message means users don't know their operations are being misinterpreted.

source_issues.title: Computer interface silently drops modifier keys (keys param) from API response
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code demonstrates that ActionClick(type='click', x=500, y=300, button='left', keys=['shift']) results in click(500, 300, left) — keys=['shift'] is silently dropped. All 5 action types (click, double_click, drag, move, scroll) are affected. The API type definitions (ActionClick.keys, ActionDoubleClick.keys, etc.) are part of the GA computer tool. Silent data loss with no warning.

signals.topic: /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests, causing indefinite blocking with no error or retry
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5 simultaneous calls), the OpenAI /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10-28% of requests with no HTTP error, no timeout, and no SDK retry. Affected requests hang indefinitely until caller timeout. This causes unpredictable latency spikes, resource waste, and potential cost loss as requests complete without result.
aliases: GPT-5.1 responses endpoint hangs concurrent requests
Silent request hangs under concurrent load
TCP connection hangs indefinitely no error returned
signals.review_reason: Significant user impact: 10-28% request hang rate under normal concurrent usage causes unpredictable blocking, wasted resources, and cost loss. User explicitly attributes to OpenAI API endpoint rather than SDK, but the hanging behavior is reproducible and documented with test data. The underlying issue affects any production deployment using concurrent requests.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: 4 reproducible test runs with 50 calls each: hung rate of 8%, 10%, 16%, 28%. Raw AsyncOpenAI client vs Agents SDK both hang at same rate (20% vs 24%), proving SDK is not the cause. TCP handshake completes but no HTTP response ever returned. No retry triggered because no error is received. Cost implications: hung requests consume resources with no result.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely with no timeout — file stuck at in_progress forever
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() has no timeout mechanism; when a vector store file gets stuck at status='in_progress' (even though the raw file is already 'processed'), the call blocks the calling thread forever with no way to recover or detect the hang.
aliases: vector store file polling timeout missing
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue: the primary API call (upload_and_poll) has no timeout and can hang forever in a non-terminal state. The user provides a concrete MRE, observed in production on April 15-16 2026. This blocks any workflow relying on vector store file ingestion.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: User reports upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely. File upload succeeds, attachment succeeds, but polling never returns. Raw file is already 'processed', but vector store file stays 'in_progress' forever with last_error=null. No timeout mechanism prevents the hang.

signals.topic: Memory leak in AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic structured outputs — unbounded SchemaValidator allocation causes OOM in long-running servers
signals.summary: When using AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models, a TypeVar resolution failure causes model_rebuild to always fail, so Pydantic allocates a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) on every parse() call with no caching. In long-running servers, RSS grows linearly with request count until OOM.
aliases: responses.parse() Pydantic schema rebuild memory leak
unbounded schema validator allocation structured outputs
signals.review_reason: Memory leak causing OOM in long-running servers is a critical reliability issue. The issue provides a detailed root cause analysis with flame graph evidence and a precise code-level explanation of why pydantic's caching is bypassed. This directly causes production crashes in any sustained-use scenario.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph provided showing memory growth. Root cause identified: TextFormatT TypeVar cannot be resolved by pydantic's model_rebuild, so _built_memo is never populated and a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer is allocated on every responses.parse() call. In long-running server: RSS grows linearly with request count until OOM.

signals.topic: Memory leak in AsyncCompletions.parse() / beta.chat.completions.parse() with Pydantic models — parsers not garbage collected across repeated calls
signals.summary: Using .parse() on AsyncCompletions with Pydantic models created dynamically via create_model() causes unbounded memory growth. Each call allocates new parsers that are not garbage collected, leading to steadily increasing RSS until process exhaustion.
signals.review_reason: Memory leak in a primary API surface (.parse() for structured outputs) causes unbounded RSS growth. User provides concrete MRE with memory profiler evidence and a functional workaround, confirming the root cause is in the library's parsing layer. This is a known ongoing issue (labels: bug, sdk) with recent activity.

source_issues.title: Possible memory leak in `AsyncCompletions.parse()`
source_issues.evidence: User provides memory profiler output showing unbounded gc object count growth across 200 calls. Workaround identified: switching from .parse() to .create() with type_to_response_format_param() stops the leak. Clear MRE with memory_profiler profile decorator demonstrating linear growth.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 — intermittent deserialization failures per worker
signals.summary: In multiprocess forkserver setups, Pydantic model deserialization intermittently raises PydanticUserError due to a hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5 walking the call stack. With DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true: ~0.6% error rate growing over time; with false: ~9.5% error rate. Affects production workloads with millions of requests.
aliases: BaseModel cannot be instantiated in forkserver workers
signals.review_reason: Intermittent deserialization failures affecting production multiprocess workloads processing millions of requests with measurable error rates (0.6-9.5%). The failure is in the library's pydantic integration path (_construct_field → construct_type → construct), not in user code. This directly impacts the main deserialization flow for chat completion responses.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: In a production forkserver setup with ~700 workers processing millions of requests: with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true error rate is ~0.6% growing over time; with false it's ~9.5%. Full stack trace provided showing _get_extra_fields_type → MockCoreSchema._get_built() → raises PydanticUserError. Related to pydantic/pydantic#11849.

signals.topic: acpx session startup destroys existing shared Codex OAuth auth when OPENAI_API_KEY is present in environment
signals.summary: Starting an acpx Codex session in an environment with OPENAI_API_KEY overwrites the existing shared Codex OAuth login on disk, causing the normal codex CLI to switch from OAuth to API-key auth permanently. This is non-idempotent and persistent.
aliases: Codex OAuth auth overwritten by acpx session startup
acpx corrupts shared Codex auth state on disk
OPENAI_API_KEY env var causes acpx to replace Codex OAuth login
signals.review_reason: User pain point: acpx session startup non-idempotently overwrites the shared Codex OAuth login on disk when OPENAI_API_KEY is present, permanently switching the codex CLI from OAuth to API-key auth. This is a session state corruption issue that blocks the user's intended OAuth workflow without any explicit action beyond starting an acpx session. Single issue from openclaw/acpx, but auth destruction is a high-severity non-blocking impact.

source_issues.title: acpx can overwrite shared Codex CLI auth and switch Codex from OAuth to OPENAI_API_KEY auth

From that point on, the normal codex CLI uses API-key auth instead of OAuth. The change is persistent and non-idempotent — the user must re-authenticate with OAuth to recover.

signals.topic: Plugin publish form rejects extensionless executables with BadHeader error — prevents publishing tools with hook scripts
signals.summary: The ClawHub web publish form crashes with HTTP 400 BadHeader when uploading packages containing extensionless executable files (e.g., shell/node hook scripts in bin/ directories). The bug is caused by the `??` operator not falling through for empty string file types, resulting in an empty Content-Type header that Convex rejects. This blocks any plugin/tool author who ships scripts without file extensions from publishing via the web UI.
aliases: publish form crashes on extensionless executables
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：publish流程是插件作者发布技能的核心路径，BadHeader错误直接导致web表单发布完全失败。虽然CLI存在workaround(zip打包)，但web UI的阻断性明确且有技术根因分析，修复方案已明确。当前只有一条issue但技术证据充分，影响所有尝试发布含无扩展名可执行文件的作者。

source_issues.title: Package publish fails with BadHeader when uploading extensionless executables
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: ?? operator in src/routes/upload/-utils.ts and src/lib/uploadUtils.ts does not fall through for empty string file.type. Result is empty Content-Type header → 400 BadHeader. Affects drag-drop publish flow only. Workaround is to zip the folder, which is surprising UX. Bug is confirmed by the reporter and linked to a specific file path and code location. Fix identified (change ?? to ||).

signals.topic: Relative reference links in skill documentation resolve to incorrect URLs, potentially redirecting users to unrelated or malicious skills
signals.summary: Because ClawHub skill slug URLs lack a trailing slash, browser relative path resolution traverses up a directory level and resolves references to unintended destinations. For example, clicking a relative link on a skill page may redirect to an unrelated skill's namespace or even a malicious skill. This is a security issue where the platform's URL structure enables cross-namespace link confusion.

signals.topic: Windows: ollama launch openclaw creates duplicate gateway process when Scheduled Task gateway already running (Session 0 isolation)

signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: a Windows user workflow that results in a critical failure state with multiple observable symptoms (port conflict, mDNS name collision, EPERM file errors, gateway closure). The duplicate process blocks the gateway from functioning correctly and requires manual remediation. Although count=1, the breadth of failure symptoms and clear user workflow impact warrant retention as P1.

source_issues.title: Remove requirement for temperature parameter for anthropic models (at least)

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Refine ignores `query_satisfied=True` when `structured_answer_filtering=True`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code demonstrates 3 LLM calls instead of 1 when Refine should short-circuit. Causes direct financial waste via unnecessary API calls and potential answer degradation.
