source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'best_of' at base.py:292. Every .complete() call crashes. Workaround requires monkey-patching. Affects all users of vLLM >= 0.19.0.

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore.query() silently ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on synchronous path
signals.summary: The synchronous query() wrapper accepts metadata_keyword_suffix but does not forward it to the async aquery() method. Custom metadata suffix support only works on the async path. Sync retrieval flows silently fall back to the default .keyword suffix with no error.
aliases: ElasticsearchStore sync query ignores metadata_keyword_suffix parameter
signals.review_reason: Silent failure in metadata filtering for sync Elasticsearch queries — users with custom metadata suffix setups get incorrect retrieval results with no error signal. Count=1, only affects Elasticsearch sync path users, so P2.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
source_issues.evidence: Parameter is silently ignored on the sync path with no exception raised. Users relying on custom metadata suffixes in standard sync retrieval flows get wrong results. Root cause identified in code (aquery call missing the parameter).

signals.topic: ReAct Agent fabricates inline citations in implicit (non-tool) responses, ignoring system prompt instructions
signals.summary: CitationQueryEngine + ReActAgent tools preserve real citations correctly, but when the agent responds implicitly (without calling any tools), it hallucinates fake inline citation tags with fabricated data. System prompt explicitly instructs to produce no citations for implicit responses, but the agent ignores this. reset() fixes it but clears chat memory.
aliases: ReAct agent citation hallucination in implicit responses
Agent generates fake citations without tool usage
signals.review_reason: Agent produces confident but factually incorrect citation data in responses where no tools were used — a core hallucination problem in a RAG framework. This undermines the reliability of agent-generated responses and cannot be fixed without losing conversation history. Meets P0 due to complete answer corruption in the implicit response path.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ReAct Agent Hallucinating Citations in Implicit Responses Despite System Prompt Instructions
source_issues.evidence: Agent fabricates complete <span class='citation-link' ...> tags with fake data in responses where no tools are used. System prompt explicitly forbids this. 8 comments indicate ongoing discussion. No workaround that preserves chat memory.

signals.topic: RvfBackend multi-writer race: deterministic silent data loss (50-87.5% at N=2-8)
signals.summary: RvfBackend in-memory snapshot-overwrite race + lock retry starvation cause silent data loss when multiple writers touch the same .rvf file. At N=2, 50% data is lost; at N=8, 87.5% plus lock crashes. Zero errors or crash signals to callers — data simply disappears. Both bugs (snapshot-overwrite in persistToDiskInner and 5-retry fixed-wait lock starvation) are fully deterministic and verified reproducible across 20 trials.
signals.review_reason: Verified deterministic data loss in core storage backend with no user-facing error signals. At N=2, half of all writes are silently discarded. The callers receive zero indication of failure, meaning users have no way to know their data was lost. This is a data-integrity catastrophe for any multi-writer scenario (multi-pane sessions, hook fan-out, swarm init). Single count is offset by extreme severity (complete silent failure of core persistence) and verified deterministic reproduction with 100% repeatability.

source_issues.title: RvfBackend: multi-writer silently loses data (snapshot-overwrite race + lock starvation) — fix included
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic: 50% loss at N=2, 75% at N=4, 87.5% at N=8; 20 trials each scenario. Callers get zero error signals — no errors, no crashes, just missing data. Fix committed in downstream fork (03ecec5e0).

signals.topic: vectorBackend controller config not passed from ControllerRegistry — 8 dependent controllers fail
signals.summary: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config to AgentDB, causing AgentDB to fall back to HNSWLib. This makes the vectorBackend controller always return null, cascading to 7 additional controllers (mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter) that all fail. Reported Activated:15 Failed:8 instead of Activated:23 Failed:0.
signals.review_reason: 8 out of 23 controllers fail due to a single missing config field, meaning a significant fraction of the controller system is non-functional. While only one issue references this, the scope of functional loss (7 downstream controllers) and the fact that vectorBackend is a core system component justify P1 priority.

source_issues.title: Bug: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config — AgentDB falls back to HNSWLib and vectorBackend controller always returns null
source_issues.evidence: 8 out of 23 controllers fail due to single missing config field. ControllerRegistry reports Activated:15 Failed:8 when it should be Activated:23 Failed:0. Cascading impact across mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter.

signals.topic: Windows Codex: first memory MCP tool call kills stdio transport — main workflow blocked
signals.summary: On Windows with Codex, the first real memory tool call (memory_search or memory_store) closes the stdio transport entirely after successful mcp_status and startup. The process appears to crash at the WASM/sql.js initialization level, below normal JS exception boundaries. After the first failure, all subsequent claude-flow/* calls also fail. This is a main-flow blocker for Windows users of the MCP integration.
aliases: Windows MCP transport crash memory bootstrap
first memory tool call stdio close Windows
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocker for Windows Codex users: the core memory functionality is completely inaccessible via the MCP interface. mcp_status works so the server appears functional, but the first real tool call crashes the transport, permanently breaking the session. Process-level crash below exception boundaries means no graceful error return.

source_issues.title: Windows Codex: first memory MCP tool call closes stdio transport after successful startup
source_issues.evidence: Windows-only crash on first memory MCP call. mcp_status succeeds but memory_search causes Transport closed. No JSON-RPC error is returned — the process-level failure is below catchable JS exception boundaries. All subsequent tool calls in the same session fail. Reproducible 100% on Windows 11.

signals.topic: MCP browser_* tools registered unconditionally — ENOENT on every call when agent-browser not installed
signals.summary: ~25 browser_* MCP tools are registered unconditionally even when the agent-browser CLI binary is not installed. Every invocation throws ENOENT via spawnSync, returning error responses and wasting tool-use turns. Tools are advertised as available in Claude Code's tool list but always fail, creating confusing UX.
aliases: broken MCP tool registration no availability check
signals.review_reason: 25 tools advertised but always failing creates significant UX confusion and wastes tool-use turns. When agent-browser is not installed, every call to 25 tools fails — this is a persistent degraded experience rather than a one-time issue.

source_issues.title: Bug: browser_* MCP tools registered unconditionally — spawnSync agent-browser ENOENT
source_issues.evidence: 25 browser_* tools advertised but always fail with ENOENT when agent-browser not installed. Model may attempt calls based on tool listing, wasting turns. No availability guard on registration.

signals.topic: getProjectCwd() prefers installer CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD over project env vars — cross-project state contamination
signals.summary: The MCP storage-path resolver in getProjectCwd() prioritizes the installer-set CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD=$HOME fallback over project-scoped runtime env vars (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, INIT_CWD). This causes session/task/agent/memory state to collapse into a shared home-scoped .claude-flow/ directory when using a global MCP installation, contaminating state across unrelated projects. Writes succeed silently in the wrong location.
aliases: project isolation broken global MCP install
CLAUDE_FLOW_CWD installer fallback too high priority
signals.review_reason: Multi-project users experience silent cross-contamination of session, task, and agent state. State from different projects merges into one shared home directory with no error or warning, and no way for users to detect the problem until data conflicts arise.

source_issues.title: MCP getProjectCwd() prefers installer fallback over project env vars, collapsing state into $HOME
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with two projects: both wrote to same /tmp/fake-home/.claude-flow/sessions/ instead of project-local paths. State contamination across unrelated repos for multi-project users. Silent failure — writes succeed, just in wrong scope.

signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked: multi-step tool-use conversations fail silently. The stream ends without completion and without surfacing an error, meaning the user has no indication something went wrong. This is a primary use case (agentic streaming) broken in a non-obvious way.

signals.review_reason: Primary use case (tool calling) is blocked for users of the GitHub Copilot API. The issue is specific enough to reproduce and affects both Claude and GPT models via the same endpoint. The downstream impact on tools like Cline CLI Kanban is noted.

signals.topic: ChatGPT Codex OAuth SSE stream crashes on truncated response.* events
signals.summary: When using ChatGPT Codex OAuth endpoint with models like gpt-5.3-codex or gpt-5.4, the backend returns large SSE events (~30KB instructions field) that frequently arrive truncated. safeParseJSON treats this as fatal and kills the entire stream with AI_JSONParseError, instead of gracefully skipping informational status events.
signals.review_reason: Stream is completely killed by a recoverable truncation error. The response.* events are informational and not needed for text streaming — the fix is to skip them rather than fail. User impact is severe: the entire stream terminates with a JSON parse error for a non-essential event type.

source_issues.title: fix(openai): ChatGPT Codex OAuth SSE stream fails on truncated response.* events

signals.topic: embed() and embedMany() crash at runtime when using EmbeddingModelV2 providers
signals.summary: embed() and embedMany() crash with TypeError when used with any provider implementing EmbeddingModelV2 (e.g. @ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.x). The doEmbed method does not return a warnings property, but logWarnings() and embed-many.ts assume it is always present and iterable.
signals.review_reason: Embedding API crashes immediately and unconditionally for all EmbeddingModelV2 provider users — a hard runtime failure on a core API. The crash is reproducible, root cause is identified, and multiple versions across the affected range are confirmed.

source_issues.title: embed/embedMany crash: 'warnings' is undefined from EmbeddingModelV2 providers

signals.topic: Deny tool approval via addToolApprovalResponse crashes with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'

Approving (approved: true) works correctly. The SDK correctly emits tool-output-denied but then fails when calling the model for the continuation step.
signals.review_reason: User-facing approval flow crashes when a tool is denied — this is a primary safety/control feature. The crash is reproducible via curl, root cause has been traced through the SDK, and both usage patterns (with/without convertToModelMessages) fail identically.

source_issues.title: streamText: deny approval crashes with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'

signals.topic: Soft navigation fails after Next.js version upgrade due to router state header parsing error
signals.summary: After upgrading Next.js server (e.g., 16.1 → 16.2), users who kept the browser tab open get a 500 error 'The router state header was sent but could not be parsed' when clicking any Link. Navigation becomes completely blocked. The router state header format changed between versions, causing server-side parsing to fail when client and server versions differ — a common production scenario during zero-downtime deployments.
aliases: Router state header parsing failure post-deployment
soft navigation breaks after Next.js upgrade
router state header incompatibility between versions
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: navigation completely fails after a deployment upgrade. This is a common production scenario (zero-downtime deploys leave clients with stale state). The error is reproducible, the root cause is identified (header format change between 16.1 and 16.2), and it has a clear user-visible impact (500 error, broken navigation).

source_issues.title: [v16.2+] Router state header was sent but could not be parsed on soft navigation with dynamic rendering
source_issues.evidence: Clicking a <Link> after a new deployment (upgrading from 16.1 to 16.2) throws 'Error: The router state header was sent but could not be parsed', navigation fails with 500 Internal Server Error. Affects all pages with dynamic rendering (e.g., root layout calling cookies()).

signals.topic: Server Action redirect() responses use 303 with chunked body, major CDN/proxies strip the body causing navigation failures
signals.summary: Next.js Server Action redirect() sends HTTP 303 with an RSC payload body framed only by Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length). Major CDN/WAF providers like Imperva strip the body on 3xx responses that lack Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding. After the body is stripped, the Next.js router receives an empty body and cannot complete the soft navigation — resulting in stale page content, failed transitions, or full hard navigations. This affects any production deployment behind a CDN that follows RFC-compliant behavior.
aliases: Server Action 303 redirect body stripped by CDN
Imperva strips body from 3xx Server Action responses
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking: navigation fails in real production environments behind CDNs that strip 3xx bodies without Content-Length. This is a well-documented, RFC-analyzed issue with HAR evidence and CDN vendor confirmation. Soft navigation fails and page content goes stale after Server Action redirects. Only excluded if the user is certain no CDN/WAF sits in front of their deployment — which is unrealistic for most production setups.

source_issues.title: Next.js Server Action redirects send 3xx responses with bodies framed only by `Transfer-Encoding`, which some proxies/CDNs strip
source_issues.evidence: HAR files and video demo show Imperva stripping the body: HTTP 303 response reaches the browser with headers intact but an empty body. Next.js router cannot complete the soft navigation, causing stale page content (e.g., header shows old postcode after form submission redirect). Imperva confirmed this is deliberate RFC-compliant behavior. Affects any production deployment behind such intermediaries.

signals.topic: OpenTelemetry fetch instrumentation permanently lost after first HMR event in Turbopack dev mode
signals.summary: When using @vercel/otel for distributed tracing, the traceparent/tracestate headers are correctly propagated on the first server-side fetch after cold start. However, after any HMR event (even a trivial file edit), the resetFetch() call permanently replaces globalThis.fetch with the pre-OTel raw fetch, stripping the instrumentation wrapper. All subsequent server-side fetches lose tracing context, breaking production-like observability in development. The regression was introduced in August 2024 and made worse in March 2026 when Turbopack App Router HMR became default.
aliases: traceparent headers disappear after HMR in dev
signals.review_reason: Significant developer experience degradation: OTel instrumentation is a critical observability tool for production debugging. Its permanent loss after HMR means developers cannot trust their dev environment to mirror production tracing behavior. The regression spans multiple Next.js versions (15.x and 16.x) and the root cause is precisely identified. Marked P1 (not P0) as it does not block production but severely degrades a critical observability workflow.

source_issues.title: `@vercel/otel` fetch instrumentation stripped after HMR in dev mode — `resetFetch()` restores pre-instrumentation fetch
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: traceparent header is present in downstream server logs after cold start, but permanently disappears after any HMR event. Not recoverable without full dev server restart. Root cause identified in resetFetch() introduced in commit 15aeb92efb and worsened by Turbopack HMR default in 0f867bb219. Affects all versions 15.5.15, 16.0.11, 16.1.7, 16.2.3.

signals.topic: Signal handling failures: SIGINT/SIGKILL/Ctrl+C not propagated to child tasks, causing orphaned processes and blocking Playwright CI workflows
signals.summary: When turbo receives SIGINT, SIGKILL, or Ctrl+C (Windows PowerShell), child processes are not terminated. SIGKILL orphans dev servers and blocks Playwright test runs (Playwright sends SIGKILL to its webServer command on exit). SIGINT/Ctrl+C leave zombie processes. Three related issues cover different signals and platforms but share the same root cause.
signals.review_reason: count=3 meets P0 threshold. All three signals (SIGKILL, SIGINT, Ctrl+C) fail to terminate child processes, which blocks the primary development loop (dev server cleanup) and automated testing (Playwright CI). Process tree screenshots and explicit Playwright incompatibility provide clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: On SIGKILL to `turbo run`, tasks continue running (incompatible with Playwright testing)

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` being sent to `turbo` is not forwarded to underlying tasks

signals.topic: Package scope incorrectly computed in daemon mode when run from subdirectory in pnpm monorepo, silently skipping tasks and producing incomplete builds
signals.summary: Running turbo from a subdirectory (e.g., apps/app1/api) with pnpm in daemon mode sometimes computes the wrong package scope, excluding 14 out of 15 packages. Cached outputs are not downloaded, tasks silently succeed with '1 successful' instead of '15 successful', and type errors go undetected. Issue is reproducible and non-deterministic.
signals.review_reason: Core build/task execution reliability is broken. Tasks are silently skipped with no error message, making the build cache unreliable and type errors go undetected. User expects 15 tasks but gets 1, with no indication of failure. This undermines turborepo's core value proposition.

source_issues.title: Tasks getting skipped with no explanation
source_issues.evidence: Running turbo tsc from apps/app1/api randomly gets scope '@riptech/app1' (1 package) instead of the full monorepo (15 packages). Debug logs show 'primary strategy timed out, attempting fallback strategy' and different package discovery results between runs. The task '//#package-deps' cache is hit but wrong packages are scoped. This is a core reliability failure of the task graph engine.

signals.topic: Turbo consumes 100% CPU and causes system-wide slowdown during monorepo builds, forcing users to fall back to pnpm -r build

A profiler trace has been captured showing the slowdown. turbo's TUI window also briefly appears for each package being built (PTY behavior not seen with pnpm).
signals.review_reason: Main development workflow is severely degraded. The system becomes unusable during builds, and the user is forced to abandon turbo and use pnpm -r build directly, negating turborepo's performance benefits. The issue affects a moderately-sized monorepo (43 packages) which is a common real-world scenario.

source_issues.title: Extremely slow with 100% CPU usage
source_issues.evidence: 43-package pnpm monorepo build with turbo 2.0.9 causes 100% CPU and system-wide slowdown. Same build with pnpm -r build uses normal CPU and does not block the computer. A profiler JSON trace is available at the linked reproduction repo. 6 comments discussing the issue.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker does not create stub files for bin entries, breaking pnpm install in Docker and blocking the recommended build pipeline
signals.summary: turbo prune --docker only outputs package.json files, omitting stub files for 'bin' entries. When pnpm install runs in the Docker container, it checks for the existence of bin entry files before creating shims in .bin, so the .bin shims are not created. This breaks downstream build tasks that depend on those shimmed CLI tools, failing the 'copy prune output -> pnpm install -> turbo build' workflow described in the official Docker guide.
signals.review_reason: The officially documented Docker CI/CD workflow is broken. Users following the official Docker guide cannot complete builds when their packages have bin entries, because pnpm refuses to create shims without the stub files present. This is a pipeline-blocking regression.

source_issues.title: prune --docker: create stub source files for bin entries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo provided showing docker build failure when dependent package produces a CLI tool. The fix is to touch stub files for each bin entry in the pruned output, so pnpm creates shims. The official Docker guide's recommended workflow is broken.

The root cause (domain operation re-evaluating unrelated production aliases) is a fundamental platform design flaw causing multi-project simultaneous outage.

multi-segment Root Directory path resolution ENOENT

signals.topic: TypeScript path aliases fail at runtime in zero-config Hono deployment on Vercel
signals.summary: TypeScript path aliases (e.g., `@/constants`) work during build but cause runtime ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors in zero-config Hono deployments on Vercel. TypeScript does not transform path aliases during compilation — the compiled JS retains `@/constants` which Node.js cannot resolve at runtime. Users must either use a bundler or manually run tsconfig-paths at runtime.
aliases: TypeScript path alias runtime resolution Hono
signals.review_reason: TypeScript path aliases are a very common DX pattern in the Node.js/TypeScript ecosystem. Zero-config deployment implies users shouldn't need additional bundling setup, yet the platform doesn't handle this transparently. This causes runtime API failures. While count=1 and a workaround exists, the gap between user expectation (zero-config = works) and reality (runtime failure) is a notable UX pain point.

source_issues.title: Runtime error with TypeScript path aliases in Hono deployment: Cannot find package '@/constants'
source_issues.evidence: Zero-config Hono deployment works for build but runtime fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when TypeScript path aliases are used. Root cause identified: TypeScript path aliases not transformed during compilation, Node.js cannot resolve @/constants at runtime. Affects Bun and pnpm. Workaround requires bundler or tsconfig-paths. Closed 2026-04-14.

signals.review_reason: User preference not honored: configured split diff view is ignored for compare marked files, forcing manual view style changes every time. Reduces productivity for users who rely on split view for file comparisons.

source_issues.title: `compare-marked-files` does not respect `diff_view_style: "split"` setting
source_issues.evidence: Setting 'diff_view_style: split' is honored for git diffs but ignored for 'Compare marked files' command (Alt+D). Always opens in unified view regardless of user preference.
